items.summary: This work considers the numerical approximation of expectations of functionals of $d$-dimensional McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations (MV-SDEs) with random initial conditions. Standard numerical schemes employ a stochastic interacting particle system of $P$ coupled $d$-dimensional SDEs, whose empirical measure converges to the MV-SDE law. However, naive Euler--Maruyama Monte Carlo (MC) estimators based on particle systems achieve a computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}\left( \text{TOL}^{-4} \right)$ to satisfy a prescribed error tolerance TOL. To reduce this complexity, this work reformulates the associated nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation as a Liouville equation describing the evolution of the law of a deterministic mean-field ordinary differential equation (ODE) with random initial conditions, sharing the same marginal distributions as the original MV-SDE. The resulting mean-field ODE eliminates the need to approximate Itô integrals and permits the use of higher-order integration schemes in time and stochastic space. However, simulating trajectories requires the score function of the MV-SDE's marginal law, which is approximated using a statistical estimator based on a system of $P$ coupled $d$-dimensional ODEs. The proposed estimator combines randomized quasi-MC in the stochastic variables and Runge--Kutta integrators in time, with efficient score estimation. Under assumptions on weak-error and variance convergence, the resulting estimator achieves a computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}\left(\text{TOL}^{-\left(\max\{β/α,2\} + 1/γ\right)}\right)$, where $α$ and $β$ denote, respectively, the weak-error and variance convergence rates with respect to $P$, and $γ$ is the order of the time-integration scheme.

items.title: From Horner's rule to neural networks
items.summary: Horner's rule is usually taught as an efficient algorithm for evaluating a polynomial. Read as a recurrence, however, it is also a small computational graph: an input is propagated through intermediate states, while parameters enter locally. This note follows that elementary observation from polynomial evaluation to polynomial fitting. The equation $Va\simeq y$ then unifies least-squares approximation, interpolation and overparametrisation as different regimes of a fixed representation. Neural networks are introduced as the next step: the representation itself becomes parametrised and is learned from data. The purpose is pedagogical rather than encyclopaedic. It offers a numerical route into machine learning, using approximation, linear algebra and optimisation as familiar entry points.

items.title: Hadwigerś Covering Conjecture in Three Dimensions
items.summary: Let $K \subset \R^3$ be an arbitrary convex body, that is, a compact convex subset of $\R^3$ with nonempty interior. We prove unconditionally that $K$ can be covered by eight smaller positive homothetic copies of itself: there exist a scalar $λ\in (0, 1)$ and translation vectors $v_1, \dots, v_8 \in \R^3$ such that \[ K \subseteq \bigcup_{i=1}^{8} (λK + v_i). \] This resolves Hadwiger's covering conjecture in three dimensions. The proof works in Boltyanski's equivalent boundary illumination formulation and is completely self-contained. Parallelepipeds are covered directly by eight translates of $\frac{2}{3} K$. For any convex body $K$ that is not a parallelepiped, we place its centrally symmetric halved difference body $S = \frac{1}{2}(K - K)$ in John's position ($B^3 \subseteq S$) and show that the spherical average of its support function satisfies $8 \int_{S^2} h_S \, d\sigmatilde < 12$, with equality only for orthogonal cubes. Using outer polyhedral approximations together with Cauchy's planar perimeter formula, the full spherical measure of directions not parallel to any boundary segment of $K$, and lower semicontinuity of curve variation, we find a unit vector $w_* \in S^2$ whose shadow boundary $\Shad{K}{w_*}$ on $K$ itself is a continuous closed curve of $S$-length strictly less than $12$. Splitting $\Shad{K}{w_*}$ into six contiguous arcs of $S$-length strictly less than $2$ and applying Helly's theorem in $\R^3$ illuminates each arc with one direction, while $\pm w_*$ illuminate the remainder of $\partial K$. The proof was discovered using an experimental harness on top of Gemini~4 Carbon and formally verified in Lean~4.

items.title: Breaking Resonance: Square-root acceleration for Metropolis-adjusted randomized Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
items.summary: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo with a fixed integration time can fail to mix because of resonances, and randomizing the integration time removes them. We prove that Metropolis-adjusted HMC with velocity Verlet and random integration times mixes from a warm start in a number of transitions that does not depend on the condition number, for every integration-time law satisfying a Fourier condition that we call non-resonant; uniform, exponential and triangular laws are examples. For a target density proportional to $e^{-U}$ on $\mathbb R^d$, where $U$ is $m$-strongly convex with $L$-Lipschitz gradient and $L_H$-Lipschitz Hessian and $κ=L/m$, the number of gradient evaluations needed to reach a fixed total variation accuracy is, up to constants and logarithmic factors, $\sqrt{κd}+\sqrt{L_H}\,(d/m)^{3/4}$. This is the first square-root condition-number bound for this sampler beyond Gaussian targets. The proof converts relative-entropy contraction of the unadjusted proposal into a conductance bound for the adjusted chain, and shows that the integration-time law enters only through its characteristic function. Hessian regularity cannot be dropped for a fixed step size: without it there are targets in the class for which the cost is at least of order $κ^{2/3}$, up to logarithmic factors, even from a warm start.

items.title: Roman Hitting Functions
items.summary: Roman domination is one of few examples where the related extension problem is polynomial-time solvable even if the original decision problem is NP-complete. This is interesting as it allows to establish polynomial-delay enumeration algorithms for listing minimal Roman dominating functions, while it is open for more than four decades if all minimal dominating sets of a graph can be enumerated with polynomial delay, or even in output-polynomial time. To find the reason why this is the case, we combine the idea of hitting set with the idea of Roman domination. We hence obtain and study a new problem, called Roman Hitting Function, generalizing Roman Domination towards hypergraphs. This allows us to delineate the frontier of polynomial-delay enumerability. Our main focus is on the extension version of this problem, as this was the key problem when coping with Roman domination functions. While doing this, we find some conditions under which the Extension Roman Hitting Function problem is NP-complete. We then use parameterized complexity as a tool to get a better understanding of why Extension Roman Hitting Function behaves in this way. We discuss another generalization of Extension Roman Domination, where both a lower and an upper bound on the sought minimal Roman domination function is provided. The additional upper bound makes the problem hard, and the applied parameterized complexity analysis provides hardness results. From the viewpoint of Parameterized Complexity, the studies on extension problems are quite interesting as they provide more and more examples of parameterized problems complete for W[3], a complexity class with only very few natural members known some years ago. We employ our findings to present polynomial-delay and FPT-delay enumeration algorithms for Roman hitting functions, also drawing the borderline between polynomial delay and transversal hardness.

items.title: Semi-Implicit Finite Volume Central Scheme for Hyperbolic Systems of Balance Laws with Adjustable Free Parameter approximation to relaxed source term
items.summary: This study develops a generalized framework for constructing a three-stage predictor-corrector finite volume scheme for solving hyperbolic balance laws with stiff relaxation source terms. The proposed scheme extends the central Nessyahu-Tadmor (NT) framework for the nonhomogeneous part of PDE and the integrals of the source terms are computed using an undetermined coefficient approach to introduce a free parameter \(α\), which offers flexibility in formulation. A unified theoretical analysis is then carried out to characterize the properties of the resulting scheme and determine the admissible range of \(α\). Specifically, uniform consistency and asymptotic properties are investigated along with $A$ -stability and $L$-stability, with the corresponding theoretical constraints combined to establish a common admissible range for the free parameter. The numerical performance of the scheme is subsequently evaluated through a sequence of test problems. Smooth-solution tests are used to assess its accuracy, while one-dimensional benchmark problems arising from different mathematical models are considered to examine its performance in comparison with existing numerical schemes. The assessment is further extended to ten two-dimensional Riemann problems to investigate the ability of the scheme to capture shocks and complex wave interactions along with computational cost.

items.title: Convergence and error analysis of problem-independent machine learning (PIML) with linear completeness
items.summary: Problem-independent machine learning (PIML) is an effective computational approach that combines the finite element method with machine learning. PIML uses neural networks to learn the mapping from material distributions or element geometries to the numerical shape functions of substructures. This approach avoids repeated computation while preserving the conformity of the underlying finite element discretization, thereby significantly improving the efficiency of substructure-based finite element analysis. However, existing studies on PIML have primarily focused on numerical accuracy and computational efficiency, while rigorous theoretical analyses of its approximation errors are still limited. In this paper, we establish an error analysis framework for PIML from a classical finite element perspective, in which the numerical error is bounded in terms of the finite element discretization error and the network generalization error. Our analysis shows that, when only rigid-body displacement invariance is enforced, the resulting error estimate contains a learning-induced term that does not necessarily decrease under mesh refinement. To ensure convergence, we propose an improved PIML scheme with linear completeness. By using linear displacement field constraints to reconstruct the corresponding columns of the transition matrix, we ensure that the resulting numerical shape-function space contains the space of linear polynomials. We derive error estimates and establish convergence results of the improved scheme in the H1 and L2 norms. Numerical experiments verify the theoretical results and demonstrate that the improved PIML achieves optimal convergence rates, good generalization performance, and numerical stability.

items.title: Linear convergence of evolution strategies to local minima by coupling with quadratic models
items.summary: Among derivative-free optimization methods, evolution strategies have emerged as competitive algorithms for multimodal, noisy or ill-conditioned problems in small and moderate dimensions. Theoretical guarantees have long been scarce, but a series of recent works established their convergence on certain classes of objective functions. A successful approach normalizes the states of the algorithm into a Markov chain and proves that this chain converges to a stationary distribution. It has yielded the linear convergence of several evolution strategies, including the state-of-the-art CMA-ES. Yet this approach requires the objective function to be scaling-invariant, hence unimodal, since otherwise the normalized process is not a Markov chain. We propose a methodology to prove linear convergence on a much larger class of functions, including smooth multimodal functions. Started close enough to a local minimum with a nondegenerate Hessian and with a small enough step size, the ($μ$/$μ$w, $λ$)-ES with stepsize adaptation converges linearly to this minimum with high probability, at the rate of its quadratic model, and the probability of failure vanishes when the initial step size and the initial distance to the minimum tend to zero. The proof views the normalized process as an adaptive chain and couples it, with high probability, with the Markov chain associated with the quadratic model.

items.title: A sharp polygonal Finsler-Hadwiger inequality
items.summary: For every simple $n$-gon of area $A$ with side lengths $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, we prove \[ \sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2 \ge 4\tan\fracπ{n}\,A +c_n\sum_{i<j}(a_i-a_j)^2, \qquad c_n=1-\frac{\tan(π/n)}{\tan(π/(n-1))}, \] with the convention $c_3=1$, so that the case $n=3$ is exactly the Finsler-Hadwiger inequality. The coefficient $c_n$ cannot be improved, and equality holds only for regular polygons. The extremal configurations are far from the regular $n$-gon: the constant is approached by cyclic polygons in which one side shrinks to zero while the others become the sides of a regular $(n-1)$-gon (a doubled segment when $n=3$). The proof combines the classical fact that cyclic polygons maximize area for given side lengths with a two variable minimization using the half central angles. We also compute the larger optimal coefficient for nearly regular polygons, and show that the best constant in the joint stability estimate for side lengths and vertex radii grows like $n^2$.

items.title: On Semilocal Convergence of a Semismooth* Newton Method
items.summary: We give conditions under which the semismooth$^*$ Newton method solves $0\in F(x)$ from a given initial point. At each step, we bound the distance from the corrected point $(x_{k+1},0)$ to the graph of $F$ by a function of the correction length. We also bound $\|A^{-1}B\|$ uniformly over the selected coderivative pairs $(A,B)$. Together, these bounds give a test on the initial graph residual and the radius of a prescribed ball. If the test holds, the iterates converge to a solution in that ball. If the decrease modulus tends to zero, every infinite run converges $q$-superlinearly. For mixed complementarity problems on a box, we assume that the smooth part has a Lipschitz continuous Jacobian and that every nonempty principal submatrix is nonsingular. We bound the error after one step for each regular pair. The bound is quadratic in the distance to a solution and depends explicitly on the norm of the correction matrix. For affine problems, we give a threshold on the norm of the vertical component of a graph point. Below this threshold, all regular pairs at that point give the same solution in one step, even when their rows come from different branches. Hence any run with vanishing graph residuals terminates in finitely many steps. For integer affine data, we give a test for an exact step using only the problem data and the current iterate.

items.title: Deterministic Distributed Graph Connectivity Sketching: Beating the Naive Sketch
items.summary: In the distributed graph sketching model, each vertex in the graph is considered as a separate processor. Each vertex is given access to its neighbourhood, and is then responsible for composing a message to a central referee, with the goal being minimising the length of these messages. Classic problems in this model include computing spanning forests, connected components and connectivity of the full graph. In the case where the vertices have to act deterministically, it has long been suspected that the correct upper-bound for computing spanning forests, connected components or connectivity would be the naive method of reporting every edge, which can be done with per-vertex message length of $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ bits. In this paper we show that this is not true for connected components and connectivity, by presenting a protocol that only requires $n/3 +3\log_{2}n$ bits per vertex for $n\geq 13$. We also show that in this setting connected components and connectivity are closely related in the required message length of the vertices. Letting $C_{cc}(n)$ be the minimum required message length in bits per vertex to compute the connected components in a graph with $n$ vertices and letting $C_{conn}(n)$ be the minimum message length to compute if the graph is connected, we show that $C_{cc}(n) \le C_{conn}(2n)$ with a multiplicative blow-up in the error probability of $(n-1)^2$.

items.title: Deterministic Polar Subcode Design via Exact Low-Weight Spectrum Characterization
items.summary: We develop a deterministic framework for improving polar-subcode minimum distance through information-set selection and dynamic frozen expression design. Expression design faces two difficulties. Changing an expression can introduce new low-weight codewords, and excluding different codewords can impose conflicting requirements on the same coefficients. To address both difficulties, we first fix the information set and release the editable frozen constraints to form a common supercode containing every candidate code. Its low-weight codewords give necessary and sufficient conditions for one coefficient assignment to exclude every codeword of the specified weights. To apply these conditions at longer lengths, we use the polar decomposition. At each split, a one in the left codeword gives two complementary output bits whose combined weight is always one. We can therefore eliminate the corresponding variables from the parity checks and count their compatible assignments to obtain the exact low-weight spectrum. With both constituent codes fixed, the same reduced checks also simplify the coefficient search. Assignments that give identical check values across all relevant messages share one representative, from which the entire group can be recovered. We give sufficient conditions for choosing the coefficients sequentially without backtracking. Finally, we use the outcome of expression design on one information set to guide exchanges of information positions for the next, linking the two design steps. In experiments spanning block lengths from 64 to 1024 and several code rates, the proposed design meets the target minimum distances in minutes and achieves competitive frame error rates under successive cancellation list decoding.

items.title: Robust decision-dependent information discovery is harder than robust optimization
items.summary: In this paper, we consider a four-stage variant of robust optimization with cost uncertainty described by the budget uncertainty polytope, known as decision-dependent information discovery (DDID). In this problem, the decision maker first queries a subset of the cost coefficients. Then, the adversary responds by revealing worst-case values for the queried elements, after which the decision maker chooses a feasible solution while facing the remaining uncertainty on the unqueried costs. Our contribution is twofold. On the negative side, we prove that, the DDID is NP-complete even when the underlying nominal problem is the 2-selection problem, for which only a polynomial number of feasible solutions exist. This contrasts with the min-max robust counterpart with budget uncertainty, known to be not harder than the nominal problem. On the positive side, we prove that the more general $p$-selection problem can be solved in polynomial time under the additional assumption that all deviations are equal.

items.title: A Fused Gaussian Process Bandit Framework for Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization
items.summary: Bayesian optimization (BO) is widely used to maximize expensive black-box functions when direct evaluation is costly. In many real-world applications, the high-fidelity objective can be approximated by a series of lower-fidelity models that provide partial but informative signals at substantially reduced cost. Multi-fidelity BO (MFBO) algorithms aim to strategically combine these information sources to achieve an optimal trade-off between accuracy and evaluation cost. However, existing MFBO methods often oversimplify the complex dependencies between fidelity levels or rely on heuristic acquisition functions that lack theoretical performance guarantees. To address these limitations, we introduce a new formulation of the MFBO problem as a fused Gaussian Process bandit and develop a corresponding Fused Gaussian Process Upper Confidence Bound (FGP-UCB) algorithm. Our approach accurately predicts the high-fidelity function by fusing multi-fidelity observations through an autoregressive Gaussian Process model and explicitly quantifies the uncertainty arising from parameter estimation across fidelity levels. The proposed method also provides theoretical simple-regret guarantees, overcoming a key limitation of existing MFBO algorithms that lack provable performance bounds. Effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated via both theoretical analysis and empirical studies.

items.title: coherent4cast: Coherent Survival Modelling and Forecasting for History-Dependent Recurrent and Terminal Events in R
items.summary: Researchers studying recurrent events and terminal outcomes need software that connects incomplete event histories to interpretable forecasts and uncertainty estimates. We present coherent4cast, an R package for fitting history-dependent recurrent and terminal event models, predicting future event burden and terminal-event risk, and assessing sensitivity to incomplete observation. Users supply event histories, covariates and observation information; the package returns fitted models, dynamic forecasts, uncertainty summaries and diagnostic measures under explicitly stated assumptions. The package integrates over event histories compatible with tied dates or observation windows and supports several frailty distributions for between-subject heterogeneity. A shared probability model generates recurrent-event counts, terminal-event probabilities and restricted mean time alive. Cross-fitted targeting provides influence-function diagnostics and asymptotic inference in supported missing-at-random and right-censoring settings. Separate sensitivity analyses provide bounds under specified recording restrictions. A baseline binary-treatment interface estimates standardized treatment contrasts under consistency, conditional exchangeability, positivity and independent censoring. A C++17 computational core supports the R interface. Independent numerical checks, computational benchmarks, simulation experiments and reproducible examples document accuracy, performance and inferential limitations. Outputs retain observation assumptions, convergence information and numerical diagnostics. The package, tutorials and replication materials are publicly available, supporting transparent analysis across clinical and other event-history applications.

items.title: KKT Atlas: Learning Low-Dimensional Local Scenario Models for Contextual Stochastic Optimization
items.summary: In contextual stochastic optimization, integrated learning trains conditional models on operational loss, but repeatedly solving stochastic programs with many scenarios is costly. We propose KKT Atlas, which partitions contexts into local charts and identifies a low-dimensional subspace per chart from decision gradients of the scenario cost. It generates shared scenarios by jointly fitting subspace coordinates and context-dependent probabilities. We show that one more scenario than the subspace dimension suffices to approximate the conditional Karush-Kuhn-Tucker optimality condition under regularity conditions, yielding decision and risk bounds under local strong convexity, with generalization error scaling with the compact parameter dimension. On three synthetic problems, Atlas uses 4-18 scenarios per decision versus 500 for direct-solve full-support integrated learning. It attains comparable or lower risk with about $4$-$23\times$ construction and $13$-$61\times$ batch deployment speedups. Atlas also achieves lower risk than clustering-based reduction at matched support budgets. In real-world European grid reserve commitment, Atlas compresses 728 scenarios to 8-9, cutting construction and deployment times by factors of about 4 and 3 relative to full-support integrated learning. Its loss is lowest over 11 quarters and, over 17 later quarters with fixed settings, slightly higher than with full-support integrated learning and significantly lower than with the remaining benchmarks.

items.title: Learning Linear Time-Varying Koopman Models for Constrained Nonlinear Optimal Control
items.summary: This paper presents a learning-based Koopman framework for solving constrained nonlinear optimal control problems. Despite significant advances in Koopman-based modeling and control, challenges remain in achieving accurate representations of controlled nonlinear dynamics and constraints while maintaining computational efficiency for optimal control. Motivated by these challenges, a linear time-varying (LTV) Koopman representation is developed to provide a more expressive representation of controlled nonlinear dynamics while preserving a linear prediction structure suitable for efficient convex optimization. Modeling errors and their propagation over extended prediction horizons are analyzed, motivating a neural-network-based Koopman framework that jointly learns lifted dynamics and constraint representations with stability-oriented regularization to improve long-horizon prediction performance. Based on the learned Koopman model, the original constrained nonlinear optimal control problem is reformulated as a convex quadratic program with conservative constraint tightening to account for modeling uncertainty during constraint enforcement. Numerical results on a low-thrust orbit transfer problem and a Mars entry guidance problem demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in terms of prediction accuracy, computational efficiency, and constrained optimal control performance.

items.title: The Anatomy of Piecewise-Linear Learned Indexes
items.summary: Piecewise-linear approximation (PLA) learned indexes (PGM-index, FITing-Tree, RadixSpline, PLEX, PLIN) compress sorted keys into $\pm\varepsilon$ segments, yet prior theory stops at coarse $Θ(\varepsilon^2)$ single-segment bounds. At the bottom layer, optimal greedy PLA covers $κ_{\rm opt}\varepsilon^2/v_0 \approx 3.54\,\varepsilon^2/v_0$ keys per segment on independent gaps and $κ_{\rm opt}\varepsilon^2$ under any smooth density ($v_0=1$), while anchored and chord fitters retain $Θ(\varepsilon^2/v_0)$ coverage. Across recursive layers, a law-of-large-numbers heuristic--invoked to claim $O(\log\log n)$ height for the PGM-index--suggests summing $Θ(\varepsilon^2)$ gaps averages out fluctuations. We prove this fails under Endpoint Promotion (EP): stopping-time fluctuations reset relative gap variance at every depth, locking fanout at $C_\varepsilon \approx 19.861\,\varepsilon^2$, expected height at $\log n/\log C_\varepsilon + O(1)$, and lookup at $Θ(\log n)$. To break this barrier, Rank-Equispaced Promotion (RE) samples pivots at equal rank strides. Each stride sums a fixed number of base gaps, so relative variance decays across layers and cumulative coverage squares at each step. Expected height drops to $\log_2\log_\varepsilon n + O(1)$ on independent gaps and $\log_2\log_\varepsilon n + \log_2^+(\log n/\log(\varepsilon/δ)) + O(1)$ on smooth densities with curvature $δ$. A compact bucket directory routes across unaligned RE pivots with $<1$ extra comparison per layer on average, giving RE-PGM $O(\log\varepsilon \cdot \log\log_\varepsilon n)$ expected lookup in $Θ(n/\varepsilon^2)$ space and $O(n)$ build time without radix skew sensitivity. Our constants match empirical fanout within $0.3\%$ down to $\varepsilon=2$, and all core theorems are formalized in Lean 4.

items.title: Minimizing Total Busy Time with Bounded Parallelism: A $3/2$-Approximation for Parallelism Two and a Forest Characterization for General Parallelism
items.summary: We study the minimum total busy time problem: jobs with fixed processing intervals must be assigned to identical machines, each of which can process at most g jobs at a time, so that the total time during which the machines are busy is minimized. The problem is NP-hard already for g=2, and, to the best of our knowledge, no approximation ratio below 2 was known for general instances with g=2, where the ratio 2 is attained by giving every job its own machine. We present a combinatorial 3/2-approximation algorithm for g=2. The algorithm applies the two-phase local-ratio technique to the known pair formulation of the problem, processing the overlapping job pairs in order of the right ends of their overlaps. The cost of its schedule is at most $L-λ/2$, where L is the total processing time and $λ$ is the optimal value of the linear relaxation of the pair formulation; hence the integrality gaps of this relaxation and of the configuration LP are at most 3/2. The result extends to temporal bin packing with items larger than one third of the bin capacity. For general g, we show that optimal schedules correspond exactly to maximum-weight forests of a special kind, which we call g-caterpillar forests; this yields an exact integer program and a linear relaxation of polynomial size for every fixed g. We also observe that securing a (1-1/g) fraction of the optimal savings suffices for a (2-1/g)-approximation. On random instances with g=2, evaluated with exact optima or tight lower bounds obtained from the pair formulation, the average ratio of the algorithm to the optimum is at most 1.075 for 100 jobs and at most 1.070 for 200 jobs.

items.title: A Unit-Gradient Neural Variational Method for Anisotropic Eikonal Equations
items.summary: We develop a variational neural method for computing viscosity solutions of the anisotropic eikonal equation. Building on the vanishing-viscosity principle, we minimize an energy functional whose Euler--Lagrange equation is the viscous anisotropic eikonal equation and introduce an auxiliary variable for the gradient, enforcing the constraint through a penalty. A key challenge in this formulation is to handle nonlinearity of the functional while controlling the interaction between the viscosity and penalty parameters. To address this challenge, we impose a unit-norm constraint on the auxiliary variable exactly, as prescribed by the eikonal equation. This removes the gradient from the exponentially weighted part of the functional and allows the viscosity and penalty limits to be studied separately. We establish two convergence results. First, for each fixed viscosity parameter $ε>0$, we prove convergence to the viscosity solution as the penalty parameter $λ\rightarrow\infty$. Second, for the distance function to the boundary of a convex or smooth domain, we prove convergence as $ε\rightarrow0$ for any fixed $λ>0$. The latter result motivates our stable numerical strategy, which keeps $λ$ fixed while decreasing $ε$ whenever the training loss stagnates. The formulation is implemented using a neural network that satisfies the unit-norm constraint by construction and a mesh-free approach that evaluates the singularly scaled functional at randomly sampled points without requiring mesh refinement as $ε\to0$. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the method on diverse isotropic and anisotropic problems, including three-dimensional open-surface reconstruction from point clouds.

items.title: An Inverse-Square Gain over Threshold Rounding at Bounded Degree: Reasonable Boolean 2-CSPs and Beyond
items.summary: Bounding the number of constraints in which a variable occurs can improve the approximation ratio of semidefinite rounding. For weighted Max-Cut and Max-2-Lin(2) of degree $d$, the known gain over the worst-case ratio is $Ω(1/(d\log d))$ (Buhai, Ghoshal, Huang, Kothari, Lee, Makarychev, and Makarychev, 2027). For binary Boolean CSPs satisfying a geometric condition, the algorithm of Ghoshal, Huang, Lee, Makarychev, and Makarychev (2026) achieves $a+Ω(1/(d^4(\log d)^{7/2}))$, where $a$ is the expected fraction of the total weight satisfied by Gaussian rounding at fixed, bounded thresholds. For weighted Max 2-SAT, the same analysis gives a gain of $Ω(1/(d^2\log d))$ over the worst-case ratio $α_{\rm LLZ}\simeq0.94016567$. We give a randomized polynomial-time algorithm with guarantee $a+Ω(1/d^2)$ under a weaker geometric condition that holds for a strictly larger class of binary instances. For weighted Max 2-SAT we obtain the ratio $α_{\rm LLZ}+Ω(1/d^2)$. To improve a worst-case ratio, only the binary constraints close to equality in the baseline guarantee need to meet the new condition jointly. This gives an inverse-square gain for Max $\{1,2\}$-Horn-SAT and for positive binary disjunctions with unit clauses of either sign, each over its own sharp worst-case ratio (Brakensiek, Huang, and Zwick, 2024).

items.title: Elastic rebound in viscous fluid: an efficient rigid--elastic splitting with an asymptotic gap model
items.summary: We formulate and test a model for an elastic body that falls under gravity onto the bottom of a container filled with a viscous incompressible fluid and rebounds without topological contact. The body is a rigid body plus a small, quasi-static elastic deformation, represented by a fixed compliance operator. In the near-contact patch, the thin fluid film is described by a Reynolds equation with cavitation. This allows the use of coarse meshes that need not resolve the gap, enabling efficient simulation. The film is coupled implicitly to the elastic surface displacement and to the rigid normal motion. The bulk fluid is coupled monolithically to the rigid body. For the axisymmetric case with vertical translation, the coupled step reduces exactly to a small dense nonlinear problem for the film pressure, with the bulk eliminated through a $2x2$ affine map. The model is implemented in NGSolve and compared with the experiments of Hagemeier et al. (2021) and the Eulerian FSI simulations of Wahl et al. (2021a). For a PTFE ball the approach agrees with the Eulerian FSI to 1\%. For a soft rubber ball (St $\approx 120$) the purely elastic model gives about three times the measured rebound. Material damping is the most important missing effect: a Kelvin--Voigt compliance with loss factor $\tanδ=0.6$ gives 4.0\,mm, against 4.4\,mm measured. A planar version of the model is compared with the recently published 2D benchmark of Corti et al. (2026). The radius of the film patch is the only numerical parameter of the splitting. It is fixed by one a-priori rule for all configurations, derived from a dry Hertz estimate of the approach, and the results depend only weakly on it.

items.title: Beyond Classical Minimax Rates: Quantum Sampling in Gradient-Based Simulation Optimization
items.summary: We study gradient-based search for a class of convex simulation optimization problems with gradients estimated from noisy outputs. With independent outputs, the optimal classical convergence rate for the expected objective gap is of order $O(N^{-2/3})$, where $N$ is the query budget. We apply quantum mean estimation to paired finite differences and progressively increase their estimation accuracy as the perturbations shrink, improving the convergence rate to $O(N^{-4/3})$. Furthermore, we show that coupling nearby evaluations improves the classical and quantum convergence rates to $O(N^{-2/(3-κ)})$ and $O(N^{-4/(3-κ)})$, respectively, where $κ\in[0,1]$ describes the variance reduction in paired outputs. Thus, quantum estimation halves the accuracy exponent in query complexity across coupling orders. Moreover, we establish matching lower bounds and show that these accuracy exponents are minimax optimal for fixed decision dimension, even when query locations and batch sizes are adaptive. Reconstruction from feasible differences retains the exponents when every simulation query must be feasible and accommodates boundary optima.

items.title: Driver Surge Maps for Supply Rebalancing with Downstream Matching
items.summary: Ride-hailing platforms use driver-facing surge maps to rebalance spatial supply by offering zone-level bonuses. These bonuses can reshape supply by inducing nearby drivers to relocate and encouraging latent drivers to become dispatchable, but both responses are voluntary. Within short decision windows, platforms risk offering bonuses that reshape driver supply without generating sufficient downstream matching value to justify the associated payments. We formulate the driver surge map design problem (DSMDP) to optimize zone-level bonuses while anticipating voluntary driver responses and downstream matching. To assess how bonus adjustments affect net operating profit, we conduct a marginal analysis that identifies when small bonuses improve on the no-bonus map and how spatial smoothness links bonus decisions across zones. Using these marginal values, we develop an iterative solution approach (ISA) to sample dual sensitivities of the matching linear program across nearby matching regimes and guide real-time bonus updates. Theoretical analysis provides certificates of approximate stationarity and establishes conditions for stationary limits. Computational experiments show that ISA improves net operating profit over the best-performing feasible benchmark by up to 19.37% on the generated instances and by up to 8.43% in the New York City study. Local shortage alone is not a sufficient basis for bonus allocation. Platforms should target responsive supply whose downstream matching value justifies the associated bonus payments. Latent-driver activation can support higher-value matches even when all demand is served, but the resulting gains must also cover additional payments to drivers who would already be matched without incentives. Results indicate diminishing returns to bonus spending and show that moderate spatial smoothness can preserve most of the gains from spatial targeting.

items.title: Blow-up size for the noncommutative rank of linear symbolic matrices with low-rank coefficients
items.summary: The noncommutative rank (nc-rank) of a linear symbolic matrix $A = A_0 x_0 + A_1 x_1 + \dots + A_m x_m$ is the supremum of $1/k$ times the rank of the $k$-th blow-up $\sum_i A_i \otimes X_i$ of $A$, where $X_i$ are $k \times k$ matrices consisting of distinct variables. In this paper, we show that the blow-up size needed to attain the nc-rank is bounded by the ranks of the coefficient matrices. More precisely, if $A_1, \dots, A_m$ have rank at most $r$, with no restriction on $A_0$, then the $k$-th blow-up attains the nc-rank for every $k \geq r$. This holds for rectangular matrices over an arbitrary field, and unifies and extends the known results that $k = 1$ suffices for rank-one coefficients (Lovász, 1989; Ivanyos, Karpinski, and Saxena, 2010) and that $k = 2$ suffices for skew-symmetric coefficients of rank two (Oki and Soma, 2025). We present two applications. First, if $r$ is a constant, then the nc-rank of an $n \times n$ linear symbolic matrix can be computed by a randomized algorithm with $O(m n^2 + n^ω)$ arithmetic operations over a sufficiently large field, where $ω$ is the matrix multiplication exponent. Second, the hierarchy of polytopes introduced by Hirai (2026), which converges to the nc-independent set polytope, stabilizes at the $r$-th level; this is based on a counterpart of our main result for the degree of the Dieudonné determinant.

items.title: A new angle on matrix-vector complexity
items.summary: The theory of worst-case matrix-vector complexity has been useful for guiding the design of fast linear algebra algorithms. However, there is a large theory-practice gap in the study of *one-sided* methods, which use matrix-vector products with $\mathbf{A}$ but not $\mathbf{A}^\top$. In practice, for fundamental problems like solving linear systems, one-sided methods like GMRES are often the fastest. By contrast, worst-case analysis often shows pessimistic results, for instance showing that one-sided methods cannot solve a linear system with ideal condition number 1 unless they read the whole matrix $\mathbf{A}$. Such worst-case complexity results do not reflect real-world experience. To address this issue, this paper proposes a different theory of worst-case matrix-vector complexity that includes information on the positioning of the eigenvalues of $\mathbf{A}$ *in the complex plane*. Specifically, we characterize the "well-behavedness" of a matrix $\mathbf{A}$ through its *spectral condition number* $κ$ and its *angular eigenvalue gap $θ$*, the angle of the largest sector not containing an eigenvalue. Under these parameters, we show that the one-sided complexity of the linear system problem is $Θ(θ^{-2}κ^{π/θ})$. These results interpolate between known results for positive definite matrices ($θ= 2π$), symmetric indefinite matrices ($θ= π$), and general matrices ($θ= 0$). This provides a rigorous explanation for the success of one-sided methods in practice, as it shows that one-sided methods beat the "optimal" two-sided algorithm (CGN) when the eigenvalues of $\mathbf{A}$ lie in less than half of the complex plane ($θ> π$). Our analysis relies on tools from numerical analysis, complex analysis, and information-theoretic complexity, and the results are presented in a modular way to facilitate future use.

items.title: A Spectral Zoo of Genus-Zero Free Boundary Minimal Surfaces with Many Boundary Components
items.summary: We study critical points of the length-normalized first Steklov eigenvalue $\barσ_1$ on genus-zero surfaces with $b$ boundary components. By a theorem of Fraser and Schoen, their first eigenfunctions give free boundary minimal surfaces in the unit ball. After uniformization, the domain is the round sphere minus $b$ round caps, with a weight on the boundary circles. A layer potential formulation gives the eigenvalues, their derivatives and a certificate for each critical point, and an exact multipole system for the caps. We compute a spectral zoo of 268 numerically certified critical points with up to $b=2252$ boundary components, including the $27$ embedded examples listed by Schulz. With their symmetry groups and Morse indices, the critical points satisfy a signed count for $3\le b\le10$. Most belong to families built from rings of boundary components. As the rings fill in, these appear to converge to the free curve minimal surfaces of Karpukhin and Noutchegueme, unions of flat disks and catenoidal annuli that meet along circles on the sphere. We construct these limits, among them the critical drum and the cake stand, a flat disk with a catenoidal horn. The families approach their limits like $j^{-1}$ for rings of $j$ caps, and the equatorial family approaches $4π$ with deficit $4πb^{-1}e^{-b}$. For large $b$, the leading terms of the multipole system reduce to the logarithmic energy of the cap centers and a formal evaluation gives $\barσ_1^\star(b)=8π-16π\,b^{-1}\log b+O(b^{-1})$.

items.title: Symmetry-reduced High-index Saddle Dynamics for Saddle Point Search under Continuous Symmetries
items.summary: For energy invariant under continuous symmetries, critical points may form critical manifolds, leading to degeneracy of the Hessian. In such cases, the ascent directions in high-index saddle dynamics (HiSD) may include symmetry directions, making it difficult to locate saddle points of a prescribed Morse index. To address this issue, we propose symmetry-reduced HiSD (SR-HiSD) by formulating the quotient HiSD on the quotient manifold and horizontally lifting the dynamics to the ambient Hilbert space. Under suitable regularity and Morse--Bott assumptions, we establish local exponential stability of the quotient HiSD equilibria associated with the prescribed index and instability of equilibria associated with critical points of different indices. We further prove local convergence of the SR-HiSD position trajectory to a single point on the target critical orbit. Numerical algorithms with direction updates restricted to the horizontal space are developed. Numerical experiments on Morse clusters, the Onsager model, and the Landau--Brazovskii model demonstrate reliable searches for saddle points of the prescribed index and the construction of solution landscapes, together with improved computational efficiency in large-scale problems.

items.title: Linear-Quadratic Graphon Mean-Field Games in Hilbert Spaces and Applications
items.summary: This paper investigates a class of linear-quadratic graphon mean-field games (LQ-GMFGs) in Hilbert spaces, where heterogeneous agents are distributed over large networks. A distinguishing feature of our model, compared with the model of well-studied finite dimensional LQ-GMFGs, is that the dynamics of agents are governed by infinite dimensional stochastic evolution equations (SEEs) involving an unbounded operator. The diffusion coefficients are allowed to depend on the state, the control, and the weighted state-average. In addition, the parameters in cost functionals could be indefinite. As the number of agents, $N$, tends to infinity, following the Nash certainty equivalence methodology, the solvability of the limit GMFG is reduced to that of an operator-valued Riccati equation and a GMFG equation system. The existence of a strongly regular solution to the former is characterized by an equivalent, easily verifiable condition, and the sufficient conditions are established for the solvability of the latter by applying the spectral decomposition method. Therefore a Nash equilibrium for the limit game is obtained. Under some adequate convergence assumptions, a set of decentralized strategies for the $N$-agent game is designed based on the Nash equilibrium of the limit GMFG, and the obtained strategy profile is shown to constitute an $ε$-Nash equilibrium. Finally, the theoretical results are applied to an optimal investment problem with delay in a competitive environment.

items.title: Upwind finite element approximation of the gradient blow-up time for a viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation
items.summary: We analyze an upwind finite element method with piecewise linear elements for a viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation with a superquadratic gradient source term, subject to homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. On polytopal inner approximations of smooth bounded domains in dimensions $N=1,2,3$, we prove maximum-norm convergence of the numerical solution to the exact solution before gradient blow-up and convergence of gradient-threshold times to the blow-up time under explicit mesh and regularity assumptions. We also verify the regularity assumption and finite-time gradient blow-up for an example on the disk, to which the main theorem therefore applies. Numerical experiments illustrate this gradient blow-up.

items.title: Robust Estimators for Stochastic Model-Based Derivative-Free Optimization
items.summary: Derivative-free optimization (DFO) methods are popular for solving stochastic optimization problems, with model-based methods being a practically successful class of DFO algorithm. In most existing works, sufficiently accurate objective estimates (used for model construction and to test for sufficient decrease) are constructed by taking a sample mean of several noisy evaluations. In this work, we demonstrate that using robust estimators (specifically the median, trimmed mean, and median-of-means) can improve the sample complexity of model-based DFO methods. Our numerical results demonstrate that robust estimators are also a practical choice for algorithm implementations.

items.title: On the computation of Green's function in layered elastic media
items.summary: We develop a recursive scheme for the computation of Green's function for time-harmonic elastic wave in three-dimensional layered media, based on a matrix basis representation in the Fourier domain and a classic interface reaction-transmission theory. With transversal rotational symmetry preserved, the scheme decouples the Green's function into SH waves and P-SV waves using five scalar functions, which are recursively solved at linear cost with respect to the number of total layers, regardless of the layers the source and target particles locate in. The resulting scheme leads to a stable numerical method ready for Hankel transform evaluation in the spatial domain, constituting a foundation for the analysis and efficient numerical simulation of elastic wave scattering in layered media.

items.title: Multi-User Linear Precoder Optimization for Obfuscation-Aided Mixed Regular and Wiretap Coding
items.summary: Physical-layer security has attracted considerable research interest with the development of quantum computing. One prominent approach is wiretap coding, which exploits the channel advantage of a legitimate receiver over an eavesdropper to achieve secure communication. However, under unfavorable channel conditions, wiretap coding can significantly reduce the achievable rate compared to regular channel coding. Mixed coding alleviates this limitation by using wiretap coding to protect a short secret required for obfuscation, while the obfuscated payload is encoded using regular channel coding. In this work, we propose a generalized obfuscation-aided mixed-coding system based on the multi-user (MU)-linear precoding (LP) architecture that unifies existing approaches employing different obfuscation functions. We then formulate the corresponding precoder optimization problem, abstracting the obfuscation function through a minimum secrecy rate constraint. Numerical simulations using a geometric two-user line-of-sight (LoS) channel demonstrated how the minimum secrecy rate requirement determines the operating point of mixed coding between regular and wiretap coding. Subsequent beampattern analysis revealed a key synergy between mixed coding and precoding: Mixed coding enables individual beam shaping for the two coding layers. Finally, spatial analysis showed that mixed coding offers the largest sum-rate gains when users are positioned at similar angles.

items.title: Breaking the Square-Root Space Barrier for Longest Increasing Subsequence
items.summary: For every fixed constant $\varepsilon>0$, we give deterministic algorithms for computing the length of a longest increasing subsequence (LIS) and for outputting an LIS in input order, both in $O(n^{2+\varepsilon})$ time and $O(\sqrt n/2^{δ\sqrt{\log n}})={\rm o}(\sqrt n)$ bits of working space for some constant $δ>0$. The input is read-only and the output is write-only. This answers an open question of Kiyomi et al. Our construction combines small-pile skipping with recursive blockwise computation of pile tops. Balanced reconstruction uses streaming intersections of forward and backward piles.

items.title: Viscosity Solutions of Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Integro-Differential Equations with Non-Lipschitz Running Costs
items.summary: We study a class of parabolic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) integro-differential equations arising from stochastic recursive control problems with jumps. These equations involve a Lévy-type operator and an additional nonlocal term in the running cost. The underlying backward generator satisfies a monotonicity condition with polynomial growth in the backward variable and is uniformly continuous, but not necessarily Lipschitz continuous, in the state, Brownian, jump and control variables. We establish well-posedness, comparison and stability results for the corresponding backward stochastic differential equations with jumps, and derive a dynamic programming principle for the associated recursive control problem. Using approximation arguments and the stability of viscosity solutions, we show that the value function provides a viscosity solution of the HJB integro-differential equation. We further establish a comparison principle for bounded sub- and supersolutions and uniqueness within a prescribed growth class, under an additional uniform bound on the jump amplitudes.

items.title: A Sequential Quadratic Programming Perspective on Optimal Control
items.summary: This paper investigates the relationship between the iterative Linear Quadratic Regulator (iLQR), Differential Dynamic Programming (DDP), and Newton's method for optimal control problems. Using a unified Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP) framework, we introduce Newton-LQR, a Riccati-based algorithm that solves for the exact Newton step the optimal control problem. Within this framework, we establish that iLQR is a principled modified SQP method rather than merely an approximation of DDP. We show that iLQR generates a descent direction, whereas the inclusion of dynamics Hessians in DDP and Newton-LQR may lead to indefinite quadratic subproblems and necessitate regularization. We further distinguish DDP and the proposed Newton-LQR algorithm through their treatment of costate information and second-order dynamics terms. Numerical experiments across six benchmark problems demonstrate that iLQR often exhibits superior convergence during the initial optimization phase, while Newton-LQR and DDP can exploit second-order information to accelerate convergence near a solution.

items.title: A Correlative-Sparse Matrix Positivstellensatz under Pointwise Commutation
items.summary: The scalar Positivstellensatz adapted to correlative sparsity enables substantially smaller moment--SOS relaxations for sparse polynomial optimization. Its matrix counterpart, however, fails in general, even under the running intersection property and local Archimedean assumptions. In this paper, we establish a matrix Positivstellensatz under these assumptions and an additional pointwise commutation condition. Specifically, if a polynomial matrix admits a decomposition whose summands commute pairwise on the feasible set, then positive definiteness on this set implies membership in the sum of the local matrix quadratic modules. The proof uses central common lower envelopes to derive an integral inequality for positive matrix-valued clique measures with consistent separator marginals, without requiring these measures to admit a global extension. We apply this result to establish asymptotic convergence of the corresponding sparse moment--SOS hierarchy for polynomial matrix optimization. We also derive a criterion for finite convergence of moment relaxation and extraction of a global minimizer based on local flatness and consistency of the local representing matrix measures on overlapping variable blocks. Finally, we provide a sufficient construction of commuting decompositions through linear equations, using a reference polynomial matrix with a simple spectrum at some point.

items.title: Bounds on the Distance of Subgradient Trajectories to the Optimal Set
items.summary: A subgradient method with a constant step size may reach a minimizer and subsequently move away from it. Thus, a bound on the best objective value does not characterize the remainder of the trajectory. In this manuscript, we first establish that the trajectory enters a near-optimal sublevel set in finitely many iterations. We then use the Hausdorff distance between this sublevel set and the optimal set to bound the distance of every subsequent iterate from the optimal set. For objectives with weak sharp minima, we derive a tighter bound and construct examples demonstrating that the bound is tight. Numerical experiments confirm these theoretical results and illustrate when the bounds are conservative.

items.title: Joint Trajectory and Power Optimization for Movable-Antenna-Aided Secure Transmission
items.summary: This paper investigates joint trajectory and power optimization for movable antenna (MA)-aided secure transmission, where the MA can transmit during its movement. Specifically, the average secrecy rate is maximized subject to movement and power constraints, which couple the MA positions and transmit powers over time, respectively. To tackle this nonconvex problem, we first decouple the transmit powers via Lagrangian duality, where the optimal power for a given trajectory is derived in semi-closed form and shown to depend only on the current MA position. Accordingly, we decouple the MA positions by equivalently reformulating the problem on a discretized linear rail in terms of the farthest grid point and the number of time slots spent at each grid point. Then, from strong duality of the convex relaxation for each farthest point, we construct an asymptotically optimal solution in which the MA dwells at no more than two positions. Finally, a low-complexity dual-based branch-and-bound algorithm is developed to select the farthest grid point and certify the optimality gap. Simulation results show that the proposed design outperforms the benchmark schemes.

items.title: Solving (Vertex-Weighted) Directed Multiway Cut Faster Than $2^n$
items.summary: In the Directed Multiway Cut problem, we are given a directed graph $G=(V,E)$ and a subset $T\subseteq V$, called the terminal set. The aim is to find a minimum-cardinality set $S\subseteq V\setminus T$, such that after deleting $S$, no directed path exists from one terminal to another terminal in the remaining graph. It had been an open question whether \textsc{Directed Multiway Cut} can be solved faster than the trivial running-time bound $O^*(2^{|V|})$. In this paper, we provide a positive answer to this question, presenting an algorithm with a running-time bound $O(1.9967^{|V|})$. The algorithm can also be modified to solve the weighted version (each vertex having a positive weight) in $O^*(1.9985^{|V|})$ time.

items.title: Verified two-sided bounds for the inf-sup constant of the divergence on planar polygons
items.summary: The inf-sup constant $β(Ω)$ of the divergence governs the stability of the Stokes problem. For polygons, analytic lower bounds are far from the true value, and numerical methods either bound $β$ from above or require spectral-gap and mesh-fineness hypotheses that cannot presently be checked. We propose a method that produces verified lower bounds without any such hypothesis. It rests on the Friedrichs formulation of $β$ in the Bergman space and on a multiplier identity that controls the non-compact corner contribution pointwise, with the sharp corner constant; the remaining compact part is bounded by a finite matrix inequality that is checked in exact and ball arithmetic. We prove that the bounds converge to $β$. Together with enclosed Rayleigh quotients of explicit trial functions (and, for the square, the bottom $\frac12-\frac1π$ of the essential spectrum) this yields two-sided enclosures, e.g.\ $0.426245\leβ\le0.426252$ for the square and $0.303973\leβ\le0.304078$ for the L-shaped domain. For a square with a square hole, which is neither simply connected nor star-shaped, we obtain $0.154596\leβ\le0.154781$. For the rectangles $(0,1)\times(0,r)$ we enclose $β$ for eight aspect ratios and prove for the five ratios $r\in\{\frac14,\frac38,\frac12,\frac9{16},\frac58\}$ that $β^2$ is an isolated eigenvalue below the essential spectrum; the last two lie beyond the range covered by the explicit bound of Costabel, Crouzeix, Dauge and Lafranche. As an application, the certified values give guaranteed a posteriori bounds for Taylor--Hood approximations of the Stokes equations, including the doubly connected domain, for which, to our knowledge, no explicit lower bound for $β$ had been available.

items.title: An Order-Optimal Square-Root Bound for Online Maximin Share Allocation with Known Types
items.summary: An allocator knows the indivisible goods, the number $n$ of agents, and the $k$ possible additive valuations. Each agent reveals their type on arrival and must immediately receive an irrevocable bundle. Kulkarni, Mehta, and Shahkar established a deterministic guarantee of $1/k$ of maximin share (MMS) and an upper bound of $2/(\sqrt{k}-2)$ for $k>4$. We determine the optimal order $Θ(k^{-1/2})$ by constructing a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm, Single-or-Select. On every arrival sequence, it gives each agent a fraction $(1/\sqrt{2}-o(1))/\sqrt{k}$ of their truncated proportional share. This share dominates MMS and is the largest target $y$ for which the item values capped at $y$ sum to at least $ny$. By specializing the construction of Kulkarni et al. to two arrivals and counting its types exactly, we sharpen the upper bound to $(\sqrt{2}+o(1))/\sqrt{k}$ even for binary valuations. For two arrivals with binary valuations and every $k\ge2$, the optimal fraction is $1/p$, where $p$ is the largest integer with $1+\binom{2p}{2}\le k$. In particular, up to six binary types permit full maximin share. For two arbitrary additive types, a different polynomial-time algorithm guarantees $4/7$ of maximin share for any number of agents. This ratio is tight for the algorithm. With three arrivals and two types, the optimal deterministic fraction is exactly $9/10$. For randomized policies with $k$ known additive types, the optimal MMS fraction guaranteed to all agents with probability at least $1-δ$ on every fixed arrival sequence is $Θ(\max\{k^{-1/2},\sqrtδ\})$ for $0\leδ<1$.

items.title: A mixed-primal FEM for Poisson-Fermi interfacial problems
items.summary: This paper presents a mixed-primal FEM for a linearised Poisson--Fermi interface problem arising from the Bazant--Storey--Kornyshev theory, which describes electrostatic interactions in ionic solutions. It leads to a transmission problem coupling a fourth-order equation in the solvent region with a second-order equation in the solute region. To precisely compute the electrostatic stress and the interactive force in the electrolyte, we reformulate the fourth-order problem as a mixed system by introducing the gradient of the electrostatic potential, the divergence of its gradient, and the gradient of its divergence as additional independent variables. The second-order problem is studied in its primal form as this approach eliminates the requirement for Lagrange multipliers to enforce the transmission conditions. The resulting formulation is discretised using Raviart--Thomas finite elements for the vector variables and piecewise polynomial finite elements for the scalar variables. Well-posedness of the mixed-primal formulation and optimal a priori error estimates for the field variables as well as for the postprocessed Maxwell tensor are established under suitable regularity assumptions, in parameter-weighted norms in which the inf-sup constant is independent of the correlation length and of the permittivity ratio. The constants in the error estimates are independent of both parameters as well, up to a loss of at most half an order when the mesh does not resolve the length scale (square root of the relative permittivity); the Sobolev norms of the solution may still depend on the parameters through boundary layers. The postprocessed Maxwell stress converges with optimal order on quasi-uniform meshes, except for the lowest-order scheme in 3D. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the properties of the proposed method for problems in 2D and 3D.

items.title: Dynamic Emulation for Bayesian Inverse Problems in Spatiotemporal Mechanistic Models
items.summary: Calibrating a spatiotemporal mechanistic model to field data is a Bayesian inverse problem in which every likelihood evaluation needs a simulator run. The R package *spDBL* replaces the simulator with a dynamic emulator, a matrix-variate dynamic linear model with a closed-form posterior that evolves the field in discrete time and processes large grids in spatial blocks. It then calibrates the parameters without further simulator runs, using Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (implemented in the Stan programming environment) conditionally on emulator draws. In benchmarks on epidemic fields, with every method tuned alike, *spDBL*'s predictions at untried inputs were the only ones with near-nominal interval coverage, though a tuned *RobustGaSP* was more accurate, and *spDBL*'s calibrations matched the accuracy of *RobustCalibration* with higher, though below nominal, interval coverage (80% against 67-76%) and over 50 times more effective samples per CPU second.

items.title: Online Statistical Inference for Derivative-Free Constrained Stochastic Optimization
items.summary: We study statistical inference for nonlinear equality-constrained stochastic optimization problems in settings where derivative information is unavailable or expensive to obtain. While recent advances in stochastic sequential quadratic programming (SSQP) have enabled efficient online optimization, existing methods either rely on gradient information or suffer from high computational costs. To address these limitations, we develop a sketched derivative-free SSQP (SDF-SSQP) method that simultaneously achieves computational efficiency and valid statistical inference. By leveraging randomized sketching, the proposed method reduces the per-iteration computational cost to $O((d+m)^2)$, where $d$ is the dimension of the decision variable and $m$ is the number of constraints, making it well suited for large-scale problems. To overcome the challenges that both sketching and zeroth-order approximations introduce for statistical inference, we adopt a random-scaling approach that eliminates the need for explicit estimation of the asymptotic covariance matrix. We establish the asymptotic normality of the averaged primal--dual iterates and construct a self-normalized statistic that is asymptotically pivotal. The resulting inference procedure is fully online, requires neither covariance estimation nor matrix inversion, and incurs an additional per-iteration cost of the same order as that of the optimization update. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of both optimization performance and statistical inference accuracy.

items.title: A Constant-Factor Single-Sample Prophet Inequality for Subadditive Valuations
items.summary: We establish a constant-factor single-sample prophet inequality for online combinatorial allocation with monotone subadditive valuations. Given one independent sample from each buyer's unknown distribution, our reduction converts any offline algorithm achieving an $α$ fraction of optimal welfare into an online algorithm achieving an $α/120$ fraction of the expected offline optimum. The guarantee holds for arbitrary arrival orders and extends to the stronger Game of Googol model. Our approach has two key ingredients: a prior-free random score generator and a new sample-based construction of tentative allocations. The tentative allocations capture substantial welfare while controlling contention for items, and the score generator relates itemwise competition in the tentative allocations to the value of retained bundles. The reduction is efficient whenever its offline allocator and score generator are efficient.

items.title: Sharp History-Length Dependence of Mesh-Uniform Exponential Decay Rates for a Boundary-Memory Euler-Bernoulli Beam
items.summary: For a boundary-memory Euler--Bernoulli beam with polynomial relaxation, we quantify the loss of exponential stability as the retained history length $S$ grows. The continuous and conforming Hermite--$\mathbb P_1$ generators have zero-frequency resolvent norms bounded above and below by constant multiples of $S$. The bounds are uniform in the beam mesh and in every history mesh of step at most a fixed $h_0$. Their semigroup norms retain a plateau of duration proportional to $S$. Under positive distributed and boundary damping, matching exponential estimates hold with the optimal time scale $1+S$, uniformly in the meshes. Optimality refers to the semigroup norm on the augmented state space, which includes the history. Without distributed damping, the same time scale holds for the continuous truncated generator under a boundary condition on $δ^{(3)}$. We also prove strong convergence of the finite-history semigroups to the full-history semigroup, uniformly on compact time intervals, under restriction and zero extension of histories. Remote-history packets give residuals of order $S^{-1}$ for the truncated generator and of order $S^{-1}+h$ after discretization, improved to $S^{-1}$ at zero frequency. Numerical tests confirm the residual orders.

items.title: Sampling Error in Time-Discretized Stochastic Optimal Control
items.summary: We study sampling error for Euler discretizations of stochastic optimal control problems driven by Brownian motion. For ordinary Monte Carlo sampling, the error can diverge under time refinement when empirical-mean fluctuations accumulate as bias. Under global Lipschitz assumptions and a bounded noise coefficient, we derive finite-sample bounds for the value-function error without assuming smooth value functions or independence across sampling batches. The bounds isolate the empirical-mean contribution. For convergence under time refinement, ordinary Monte Carlo generally requires the number of samples per stage to grow at a faster rate than the number of intervals in the time mesh, whereas antithetic and recentered sampling eliminate the empirical-mean term and yield error bounds uniform over meshes with a fixed sample size per stage. We establish lower bounds showing that the ordinary and antithetic sampling terms are attained. We also prove sample-size convergence for all three methods on fixed meshes. For antithetic and recentered sampling, convergence is uniform over meshes in every noise dimension, with sharp sample-size rates in dimensions at least three.

items.title: A Kernel Framework for Linear Operator Equations
items.summary: Solving linear operator equations with nonlocal terms or heterogeneous constraints often requires specific numerical schemes. We develop a unified approach based on embedding such equations into a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). Differential, boundary, and integral operators are represented by their Riesz representers in the RKHS. The equations are solved in the regularized least-squares sense at finitely many collocation points. The solution is a finite linear combination of operator-induced representers and is obtained from a single linear system. Its sensitivities, such as financial Greeks, follow by direct differentiation. To reduce the computational cost for large collocation sets, we introduce a Nyström approximation based on subsampling the operator-induced representers. It yields the best approximation of this solution within the reduced trial space, in a regularized empirical norm. Numerical examples cover ordinary, partial, and partial integro-differential equations, including multi-asset and jump-diffusion option pricing.

items.title: Uncertainty Quantification and Global Sensitivity Analysis of Patient-Specific Coronary Hemodynamics Under Unsteady Flow Conditions
items.summary: Patient-specific computational models of the coronary arteries demonstrate transformative potential for physiological assessment, identifying hemodynamic markers associated with disease progression, and optimizing treatment. Unfortunately, these models rarely account for input parameter uncertainty, limiting confidence in predictions and their clinical interpretation. Herein, we present a novel uncertainty quantification-finite element framework that integrates computationally efficient techniques to characterize and propagate uncertainty through patient-specific coronary simulations under unsteady flow conditions. Principal component analysis characterized variability in pulsatile coronary velocity waveforms, while uncertainty in blood pressure, viscosity, density, and heart rate is represented through probability distributions. Polynomial chaos expansion (PCE) enabled efficient uncertainty propagation and global sensitivity analysis across three patient-specific models, quantifying variability in time-averaged wall shear stress (WSS), oscillatory shear index, and cross-flow index. Fourth-order PCE emulators converged across all three patients, yielding analyses of 505 models per patient, with median coefficients of variation ranging from 0.15-0.20 for time-averaged WSS, 0.54-0.75 for oscillatory shear index, and 0.28-0.38 for cross-flow index, highlighting greater relative uncertainty in multidirectional WSS metrics. Global sensitivity analysis revealed that time-averaged WSS variability was governed by the individual effects of velocity and blood viscosity, with parameter interactions contributing <2% of total variance. In contrast, velocity waveform uncertainty dominated variability in the oscillatory shear index and cross-flow index, with higher-order parameter interactions accounting for 20.7-34.5% and 26.6-37.8% of total variance, respectively.

items.title: An augmented generalized factorization bound for generalized maximum-entropy sampling
items.summary: Li proposed an augmented factorization upper bound for use in branch-and-bound (B&B) algorithms aimed at the maximum entropy sampling problem (MESP). This bound improves on the factorization bound for MESP when the input covariance matrix is positive definite. GMESP, which selects $s$ of $n$ variables so as to maximize the product of the $t$ greatest eigenvalues of the corresponding principal submatrix of the covariance matrix, is a generalization of MESP (the case $t=s$), and the factorization bound for MESP generalizes to GMESP. We extend the augmentation technique of Li to improve on the generalized factorization bound for GMESP when the input covariance matrix is positive definite. We derive fundamental properties of the augmented bound, and we develop primal--dual constructions for use within B&B. We give checkable conditions under which the relaxation can be solved in closed form, which always hold when $t=1$, at the root and at every subproblem, and a condition under which the closed-form solution is optimal for GMESP. We compare the augmented bound with the spectral bound, establishing an exact comparison for $t=1$, an improved worst-case comparison for general $t$, and sufficient conditions for the dominance of each bound over the other. Computational experiments on benchmark instances show that augmentation can substantially reduce root gaps of the generalized factorization bound, while even reducing its computational time, and that it improves the performance of B&B. Moreover, a hybrid strategy that uses the trace upper bound to prune nodes and the closed-form certificate to avoid solving the relaxation can significantly accelerate B&B when $t$ is small.

items.title: Provably Near-Optimal PQ in the Extended Zador Model
items.summary: This paper investigates Product Quantization (PQ) Optimization with Gaussian data. It offers three key contributions (i) a proof that SVD is the optimal preconditioning rotation for PQ; (ii) a new Extended Zador (EZ) estimator of the $k$-means quantization cost that is accurate in low bit rates and low dimensions; and (iii) a novel segmentation algorithm based on 1-d bin packing of global bit allocations. The result is a simple algorithm (EZPQ) with strong approximation guarantees. It matches OPQ's empirical accuracy while providing a per-instance distortion lower bound certificate under the Gaussian EZ cost model. On typical real embedding spectra, EZPQ with 2 bits per coordinate is often certifiably within 1% of the optimum in this model. It also consistently achieves a lower reconstruction error than all random-rotation-based algorithms such as EDEN, E-RaBitQ, and TurboQuant.

items.title: An $O(n^{-1/2})$ remainder for the Chow--Robbins stopping boundary
items.summary: We sharpen the asymptotic approximation to the optimal stopping boundary in the Chow--Robbins game, proving the inverse-square-root remainder conjectured by Elton. The proof combines an exactly harmonic integral for simple random walk with a Catalan first-passage renewal identity. Averaging the stopping defect over one spatial period removes its leading lattice dependence, and a coupling of states at equal depth transfers this cancellation to the renewal sum. Consequently, the explicit integer stopping rule can fail at no more than a constant times the square root of the number of observation times.

items.title: Adaptive Robust Optimisation for Frequency-Constrained Market Clearing Problem
items.summary: This paper formulates the day-ahead market clearing as a two-stage adaptive robust optimisation problem in which the first stage determines unit commitment, energy dispatch, and reserve procurement, while the second stage represents worst-case balancing actions under simultaneous uncertainty in renewable generation, load, and HVDC converter outages. Frequency security is enforced explicitly through inertia and fast frequency response constraints at the synchronous-area level, with HVDC lines allowed to provide emergency power support within their available headroom. The resulting min--max--min problem is solved by a column-and-constraint generation algorithm and applied to an eight-country North Sea test system comprising three synchronous areas, sixteen onshore bidding zones, and five offshore wind farm hubs connected through a meshed HVDC grid. We compare the Home Market (HM) and Offshore Bidding Zone (OBZ) designs on this infrastructure across different uncertainty scenarios. The results first demonstrate the value of robustness, where deterministic solutions that ignore uncertainty are severely vulnerable to worst-case realisations. Comparing the two designs, we find that OBZ's offshore zone boundaries make line congestion visible to the day-ahead market, enabling targeted reserve procurement that raises day-ahead costs but substantially reduces real-time load shedding, yielding a net reduction in total system cost that grows with the severity of localised offshore uncertainty. When both designs face the identical worst-case contingency, HM cannot distinguish an offshore converter trip from normal operation and thus fails to hedge against it, while OBZ considers the risk at the day-ahead stage. This advantage can be seasonal, scaling with the ratio of offshore wind output to HVDC line capacity and diminishing when onshore generation dominates the supply mix.

items.title: A decoupled BDF2-type integrator for the spin-diffusion Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert system in ferromagnetic multilayers
items.summary: We propose and analyze a fully discrete, linear, decoupled BDF2-type finite element integrator for the spin-diffusion Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert (SDLLG) system arising in spintronics. The SDLLG equations couple the magnetization dynamics with a diffusion equation for spin accumulation. The proposed numerical method combines a projection-free BDF2-type tangent-plane discretization of the magnetization dynamics with BDF2 time-stepping for the spin accumulation. By treating the coupling terms explicitly through extrapolation, each time step requires only two independent linear solves that can be performed in parallel. The analysis accommodates the usual exchange field and a general, possibly nonlinear, lower-order effective field. Unconditional weak convergence towards a global weak solution is shown. We also establish bounds on the deviation from the unit-length constraint. Under additional assumptions on the associated energy functional, an energy inequality for the limiting solution is obtained. Numerical experiments support the theoretical findings.

items.title: Sampling at Scale: Distributed Multi-Agent Trajectory Optimization
