items.summary: Embedding hard operational constraints into an unconstrained Hamiltonian via large penalty multipliers induces quadratic spectral aliasing during phase estimation and increases two-qubit gate depth. This paper proposes a penalty-free, closed-loop dynamic quantum circuit scheme, designated as Zeno-decoupled gauge-ratchet optimization (Z-GRO), for constrained binary optimization without outer-loop training. Reversible feasibility phase operators within symmetric dynamical-decoupling echoes confine evolution to the feasible subspace, while an interaction-correlated commutator gauge operator resolves initial symmetry stall. Directional cooling couples the unpenalized objective Hamiltonian to a reusable ancilla with a zero-two-qubit-gate threshold offset, bypassing echoed tunneling gates on retained branches. A survival-filtered Ramsey controller advances the threshold from a linear-programming bound with automatic overshoot rollback. Exact density-matrix and trajectory simulations on spin-glass and quadratic knapsack ensembles show a single-check discrimination gain above four orders of magnitude, improving ground-state probability by factors of 3.0 to 4.3 over quantum Zeno dynamics and 11.4 to 22.5 over penalized schemes. Z-GRO reduces the spin-glass time-to-solution scaling base to 1.529 (compared to 1.684 for quantum Zeno dynamics and 1.909 to 2.047 for penalized schemes) and lowers 14-qubit knapsack time-to-solution by factors of 2.4 to 14.5. For two-qubit gate error rates between $5 \times 10^{-4}$ and $5 \times 10^{-3}$, Z-GRO achieves 2.9 to 7.0 times the optimal probability of noisy penalized feedback, while majority shielding limits loss to 6.3% at a 5.0% readout bit-flip rate, recording 0/24, 0/25, 0/96, 3/25, and 2/80 overshoots.

items.title: Stochastic Extragradient Methods Beyond Lipschitz Continuity
items.summary: Stochastic variational inequality problems have received significant attention due to their ability to model large-scale machine learning tasks. Typically, the operators involved are assumed to be globally Lipschitz, with only a handful of works extending beyond the standard setting to the so-called $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz setting. In this work, we propose a novel stochastic past extragradient algorithm for variational inequality problems under a broad regularity assumption that is even less restrictive than $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz continuity and provide convergence guarantees under bounded variance of the stochastic oracle. More precisely, we show a.s. convergence with suitable stepsize schedules and obtain convergence rates in expectation and in probability for fixed horizons. Finally, in numerical simulations we compare our proposed algorithm against standard methods.

items.title: Distributed Optimization of $M$-Convex Functions Subject to Linear Constraints via Continuous Relaxation and Shapley-Folkman Decomposition
items.summary: $M$-convex functions from discrete convex analysis admit tractable minimization and convex extensions that agree with them at integer points. We study the minimization of a separable collection of $N$ $M$-convex functions subject to $m$ linear coupling constraints. Our two-stage algorithm first solves the convex relaxation and then reconstructs an integer solution through local Carathéodory decompositions and an LP purification step. The returned solution has no objective increase relative to the convex-relaxation value and a coupling residual that is $O(m)$ for bounded coupling coefficients, with no explicit dependence on $N$. We prove polynomial value-oracle evaluation of the $M$-convex extension and give both an exact value-oracle-polynomial implementation and a distributed consensus-ADMM implementation under a proximal oracle. We also establish proximity and additive envelope-gap guarantees when Stage~1 uses a strongly convex extension. On an inventory placement problem with up to about $10^6$ products, both guarantees hold on every run, and the method is faster than exact integer-programming benchmarks by a factor that grows with the number of regions.

items.title: Convex Structure-Preserving EDMD: Passive Koopman Matrices as $Q$-Contractions
items.summary: Extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) approximates the Koopman operator using a matrix based on a finite set of observables. However, the least-squares matrix of a port-Hamiltonian (pH) system is generally neither passive nor invariant-preserving. We demonstrate that the implicit midpoint discretization of a lifted pH model precisely preserves energy balance, passivity, and all linear Casimirs for every step size. For a fixed storage metric $Q$, the resulting Koopman matrices are the Cayley transforms of $(J-R)Q$, where $J$ is skew-symmetric and $R$ is positive semidefinite. This set does not depend on the step size and is the closure of all Q-contractions. This set is LMI-representable; therefore, structure-preserving EDMD, including ports through a discrete-time Kalman-Yakubovich-Popov condition and Casimirs through affine constraints, is a semidefinite program. The constrained estimate is a projection of the unconstrained estimate in the data-weighted norm and cannot increase estimation error when the population target is pH-compatible. For every $Q$-contraction, a certified bound on the lifted prediction error grows linearly at most in time, whereas it grows geometrically for unconstrained models with Q-gain above one. Benchmarks on a damped pendulum and a damped rigid body demonstrate that constrained models never generate energy and that imposed Casimirs are maintained with solver accuracy (approximately $10^{-8}$). In contrast, EDMD may diverge or lose the Casimir with noisy data. The benchmarks also demonstrate that when $Q$ is the physical energy, the constrained models are less accurate than EDMD and can exhibit significant structural bias.

items.title: Full-chip constrained quantum annealing via self-calibrating spin-susceptibility control
items.summary: Discrete optimization in finance, power grids, and logistics requires minimizing Ising Hamiltonians under coupled linear constraints. However, quadratic-penalty formulations generate dense cliques that exhaust the minor-embedding capacity of sparse superconducting processors at 128-176 spins, and first-order dual subgradient schemes diverge or stall under constraint coupling. Accordingly, this study proposes a closed-loop primal-dual scheme, designated as Self-Calibrating Quantum Susceptibility Quasi-Newton (SelfCal-QSQN), in which linear constraints are encoded in longitudinal fields and dual curvature is reconstructed from single-shot spin-fluctuation covariances. This scheme requires no penalty couplers, slack qubits, or perturbation queries. Evaluated over 891 runs on D-Wave Advantage (5,612 qubits) and Advantage2 (4,560 qubits), SelfCal-QSQN achieves 83.3% full-chip exact feasibility, reduces high-constraint error by 6.1-20.1-fold over $K$-scaled first-order updates (138.4-323.3-fold over fixed-gain curvature), outperforms time-matched mixed-integer programming at 256 spins, and attains 95.0%-96.7% feasibility on non-native and inequality benchmarks. Moreover, the scheme is robust toward shot noise and freeze-out drift.

items.title: Coding Length and Optimal Power Allocation in Correlated Block Fading
items.summary: A codeword spans a fixed number of correlated Gaussian fading blocks. The receiver knows the gains and the transmitter knows only their law. At fixed average signal-to-noise ratio, we require the decoding error probability to decay exponentially with the number of receive antennas. When does outage predict the achievable rate? If block length grows faster than the number of antennas, outage gives the limiting optimal rate. If both grow to infinity at a fixed positive ratio of block length to array size, outage strictly overestimates the limiting rate. We determine the critical ratio above which positive rates are possible. For sufficiently large finite ratios, we find the exact limiting rate over all codes satisfying a total energy constraint on each codeword. The leading rate loss is inversely proportional to the ratio. Its coefficient depends on Gaussian channel dispersion at the most likely fade causing outage and on how quickly the outage rate decreases as the required error exponent increases. In the long-block limit, equal power loses rate on every window of three or more blocks under stationary first-order autoregressive fading with positive lag-one correlation. In a different three-block channel with identical marginal gains, tightening the reliability requirement first makes it optimal to leave the middle block unused and later to use it again.

items.title: Shellsort with $O(n\log n)$ Average-Case Complexity
items.summary: We show that Shellsort admits a fixed sequence of $O(\log n)$ gaps that sorts a uniform random permutation in $O(n\log n)$ expected comparisons. In fact, we give a distribution on decreasing gap sequences with this expected bound for every fixed input. We also give a randomized polynomial-time algorithm that, with high probability, constructs a sequence attaining the average-case bound.

items.title: On Robust Strictly Positive Real Synthesis for High-Order Interval Polynomials
items.summary: We establish two complementary results on common strictly positive real (SPR) numerators for Hurwitz-stable interval polynomial families. First, for every order $n \ge 10$, we construct a monic Hurwitz-stable interval polynomial family with rational endpoints and positive width in every nonleading coefficient such that every nonzero real numerator of degree at most $n$ produces a strictly negative real part at some member and some positive frequency. In particular, robust Hurwitz stability alone does not guarantee equal-degree SPR synthesis in high orders. Second, for every order $n \ge 1$, we prove that a common real SPR numerator of exact degree $n$ always exists whenever the lower endpoint of each interior coefficient interval is at most $10^{-5}$ times its upper endpoint, while the constant and leading coefficients vary over arbitrary compact positive intervals.

items.title: Quadratic unconstrained binary optimization benchmark problems from mixed Hamming packings
items.summary: Benchmarking exact solvers and noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices for quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) requires small yet challenging instances, preferably coming from actual applications. We propose such a benchmark set derived from mixed Hamming packing, a hard problem in coding theory. Starting from its mixed-integer linear programming formulation, we provide a generator for the equivalent QUBO models and study 133 instances whose optima are certified by that formulation. In the feature space of the MQLib library, we position a broad range of existing quantum-oriented benchmarks relative to the classical ones: they lie along a narrow, sparse border of the region covered by MQLib, whereas our instances form a coherent family in a region that both collections leave almost empty. Classical heuristics and a simulated bifurcation machine find the optimum of most instances quickly, in several cases sooner than an exact mixed-integer solver first encounters it, suggesting heuristic warm starts for exact solvers; for an exact QUBO solver, in turn, it appears challenging to prove optimality. In Ising form, the instances are densely connected antiferromagnets whose large local fields are almost exactly balanced by the couplings, so that the decision on each variable rests on a small remainder. This makes them hard to embed and to represent accurately on current quantum annealers, in line with our D-Wave experiments.

items.title: Generalized Markov numbers and plane lattices
items.summary: We give new explicit constructions of lattice rules in the two-dimensional square and torus. It is well-known that uniformly distributed lattices (in the sense of low-discrepancy) arise from continued fractions with bounded partial denominators. We demonstrate how integers solutions of the generalized Markov equation $x^2+y^2+z^2 = kxyz-k+3$ give rise to such lattices.

items.title: Linear and Quadratic Penalties for Cardinality Constraints in Unconstrained Binary Optimization
items.summary: We study penalty strategies for converting constrained binary optimization problems to quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) form on the example of the sparsest $k$-subgraph problem. We adopt an augmented Lagrangian approach involving a linear penalty in addition to the commonly used quadratic one, and show the benefits of this approach. From the constraint structure, we derive sufficient bounds on the penalty coefficients. We conduct extensive experiments comparing combinations of our different penalty strategies with a wide range of classical and quantum QUBO solvers. Our experiments show that to obtain a good-quality solution, the right penalty strategy is almost as important as the quality of the QUBO solver, and iterative approaches appear to be the most efficient. We discuss the mechanisms that lead to a degradation of the solution quality due to large quadratic penalties.

items.title: Incentive-Based Regulatory Mechanism for Tariff Design in District Heating and Cooling Networks
items.summary: Low-temperature district heating and cooling networks exchange heat bidirectionally at near-ambient temperatures. When one supplier owns the shared loop, it controls both the tariff and the network temperature that sets every user's conversion efficiency. Existing price-cap and cost-based rules leave this non-price instrument unregulated and reach neither the first-best dispatch nor an explicit division of gains. This paper proposes a two-part, incentive-based tariff that anchors the supplier's lump-sum fee, per building and hour, to an audited outside alternative and divides the participation gains through one regulated share. We model a mixed-integer bilevel Stackelberg game in which the supplier sets hourly tariffs and the temperature regime, anticipating the buildings' co-optimization of electricity and thermal exchange. We prove that the mechanism attains the first-best welfare, posts the shadow price of the efficient dispatch as its tariff, keeps every building at or above its outside option every hour, and keeps the supplier solvent whenever operation adds surplus. A Belgian case study confirms these properties. The mechanism reproduces the centralized welfare whenever operation is worthwhile, declines to operate otherwise, holds the loop at its first-best temperature, and outperforms cap-based regulation and Ramsey pricing in welfare, user protection, and cost recovery.

items.title: Scattering by two parallel semi--infinite arrays of sound--soft scatterers
items.summary: This article considers the scattering of an acoustic wave by two identical semi--infinite arrays of point scatterers which are positioned parallel to one another. The resulting system of scattering coefficients is formulated as a pair of coupled discrete Wiener--Hopf equations with a full $2\times2$ matrix kernel composed of two scalar kernel functions that represent interaction within the selected array and between the two arrays. Exploiting the symmetry of the two arrays, we introduce symmetric and antisymmetric components of the scattering coefficients, which decouple the matrix Wiener--Hopf system into two independent scalar problems with kernels given by the sum and difference of the two original kernel functions. The scalar Wiener--Hopf equations are then solved using the Wiener--Hopf technique in a very similar way to what has previously been used to solve the semi--infinite array problem. The original definitions of the two scalar kernels are represented by a lattice sum and practical evaluation techniques are discussed. Comparisons with previous work are also critically discussed. The resulting formulation provides an exact analytical solution to a coupled semi--infinite array problem and illustrates how symmetry can reduce a discrete matrix Wiener--Hopf problem to two scalar problems.

items.title: Decision trees for subword-closed languages over arbitrary finite alphabets
items.summary: Moshkov classified binary subword-closed languages $L$ by the minimum depth of decision trees that recognize the words of length $n$ in $L$, or decide membership in $L$, using queries that return the $i$th letter of the input word. We extend this classification to alphabets with $k \ge 2$ letters. With the homogeneity and heterogeneity dimensions defined via pairs of different letters, the classification is the same as for $k = 2$: the deterministic recognition depth is bounded, logarithmic, or linear in $n$, the other three depths are bounded or linear, and there are five complexity classes. Since Moshkov's two-block structure lemma fails for $k \ge 3$, we prove a structure lemma with up to $k$ blocks. Our bounds are polynomial in $k$ and the two dimensions; in the bounded case they replace the exponential constant of the binary case by a linear one. We also show that the complexity class (one of the five) of a language given by a finite set of forbidden subwords can be computed in polynomial time. For several ternary languages we prove exact formulas for all four depths and check them by computation for small $n$.

items.title: Consensus of Consensus: Decentralized Consensus-Based Optimization
items.summary: We propose and analyze a decentralized variant of Consensus-Based Optimization (CBO) for the global minimization of continuous, possibly non-convex functions accessible only through a stochastic, possibly biased, zeroth-order oracle with bounded mean-squared error. The agents are split among $N$ units of an undirected communication network. Each unit evolves its swarm of $M$ agents towards a local tracking variable, which follows the network average of the local consensus points through one round of neighbour-to-neighbour communication via a doubly stochastic mixing matrix, without any central coordinator. We show that, under an explicit condition linking the drift and diffusion parameters to $M$, all agents reach consensus almost surely, at an exponential mean-square rate governed by the spectrum of the mixing matrix. Using a finite-agent quantitative Laplace principle, we prove that, for large $α$ and provided some agent visits a neighbourhood of the global minimizer with sufficient probability, the expected mean-squared distance of the swarm from the minimizer falls below any tolerance within an explicit number of iterations, at a rate that deteriorates for poorly connected networks. We verify this hitting assumption for a simplified dynamics. Experiments on benchmarks up to dimension $d=1000$, with stochastic objectives, and on a federated learning task demonstrate the method's effectiveness.

items.title: Space-Efficient Text Indexing for Advanced Counting Queries
items.summary: In the classical problem of text indexing, the objective is to preprocess a text $T=T[1..n]$ over an integer alphabet $[0..σ)$ into a data structure that supports efficient pattern matching queries. Given a pattern $P=P[1..m]$, a reporting query lists the set $\mathsf{Occ}_T(P)$ of occurrences of $P$ in $T$, whereas a counting query returns $|\mathsf{Occ}_T(P)|$. Space-efficient suffix-tree variants use only $\mathcal{O}(n\logσ)$ bits and support reporting queries in $\mathcal{O}(m+|\mathsf{Occ}_T(P)|\cdot\log_σ^ε n)$ time, where $ε>0$ is an arbitrarily small constant, and counting queries in $\mathcal{O}(m)$ time. Notably, space-efficient indexes for more advanced counting queries have largely resisted achieving the same optimal (or near-optimal) query times when using less than $Θ(n\log n)$ bits. We change this situation by proposing a general framework that supports advanced counting queries, denoted by $φ_T(P)$, provided that $φ_T$ satisfies two mild conditions: (1) $φ_T(P)$ is an integer in $[0..|\mathsf{Occ}_T(P)|]$ that can be computed from $\mathsf{Occ}_T(P)$ via sorting; and (2) $φ_T(Q)\geqφ_T(P)$ for every prefix $Q$ of $P$. We show that our framework supports optimal $\mathcal{O}(m)$-time queries using $\mathcal{O}(n\logσ+n(\log\log n)^2)$ bits or near-optimal $\mathcal{O}(m\log_σ^ε n)$-time queries using $\mathcal{O}(n\logσ)$ bits. As an example, our trade-offs improve upon the classical MAST index for counting non-overlapping occurrences [Apostolico and Preparata, Algorithmica, 1996; Brodal et al., ICALP 2002], which uses $\mathcal{O}(n\log n)$ bits and supports $\mathcal{O}(m)$-time queries, and the recent compact index for the same problem [Bals et al., ESA 2026], which uses $\mathcal{O}(n\logσ)$ bits and supports $\mathcal{O}(m\log n\log_σ^ε n)$-time queries.

items.title: Structure-preserving compression of Matrix Product States
items.summary: Matrix product state time evolution relies on compression to control the growth of bond dimensions, but compression can break the conservation laws of the equation being solved. A truncation is not the flow of a Hermitian generator, so even a small truncation error can violate exact algebraic identities of the Schrödinger equation. For any matrix product state integrator that leaves the state in canonical form with an orthogonality center, a scalar correction restores an admissible global invariant after compression whenever the resulting scalar quadratic constraint equation admits a real root, without enlarging any bond dimension. Rank-preserving recovery searches other canonical centers when that correction fails. The geometry of the low-rank manifold provides sufficient conditions for conservation by the fixed-rank projected flow and bounds what corrections within a frozen center frame can achieve. Numerical experiments demonstrate that recovery can be required even along accurate truncated trajectories.

items.title: Structure-Preserving Model Reduction of Metriplectic Systems via Oblique Projections and Block Structure
items.summary: Metriplectic systems combine conservative and dissipative dynamics and are characterized by energy conservation and entropy production. The degeneracy conditions underlying these properties are generally not preserved by standard projection-based model order reduction. We develop two structure-preserving reduction strategies. The first enforces degeneracy conditions through oblique projections and combines gradient-preserving and matrix empirical interpolation for hyper-reduction. The second constructs reduced bases adapted to available operator block structure, preserving degeneracy without online oblique corrections. We establish sufficient conditions for preserving the Jacobi identity and derive a priori error estimates. Numerical tests on benchmark problems demonstrate accuracy, thermodynamic consistency, and computational efficiency.

items.title: A Structured Levenberg--Marquardt Method for Binary Tensor Completion
items.summary: We develop a structured Levenberg--Marquardt (LM) method with trust-region globalization for binary tensor completion, using triple decomposition and a logistic loss. Under a local component-residual error bound and positive outer curvature, we prove quadratic convergence of the exact iteration for damping exponents $1\leδ\le2$, without requiring full row rank. A constant-rank criterion and an explicit rank-one certificate provide sufficient conditions for the residual error bound. The analysis decomposes the local error into outer-loss linearization, factor linearization, and regularization contributions. For a symmetric nonquadratic logistic--LSE family with $δ=2$, cancellation improves the objective-model error to fourth order and the decrease-ratio error to second order. A synthetic experiment illustrates the local quadratic convergence rate. On the HCP and Enron datasets, the proposed method improves binary tensor completion accuracy while requiring fewer outer iterations than the first-order methods.

items.title: Balanced Boolean Functions from Sparse Niho-Type Permutation Polynomials: Few-Valued Walsh Spectra and Applications
items.summary: We study balanced Boolean functions parameterized by two-to-one mappings of the forms $P(x+x^2)$ and $P(x+x^{-1})$, where $P$ is a sparse permutation polynomial with generalized Niho-type exponents. First, for $q=2^m$ with $m$ even, we determine the complete four-valued Walsh distribution of the balanced Boolean function parameterized by $Q(x+x^2)$, where $Q(x)=x(1+x^{q-1}+x^{2(q-1)})$. We then generalize a permutation polynomial studied by Gupta and Sharma to the parameterized family $P_λ(x)=x^{3q-1}+λx^{2q}+λx^2$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. We prove that $P_λ$ is a permutation polynomial if and only if either $λ=0$, or $λ\ne0$ and $X^3+X+λ^{-1}$ has no root in $\mathbb{F}_q$. Moreover, the number of admissible parameters is $(q+2)/3$ when $m$ is even and $(q+4)/3$ when $m$ is odd. Thus, admissible parameters exist for every $m\geq2$, and approximately one-third of the elements of $\mathbb{F}_q$ yield permutation polynomials. For every admissible parameter $λ$, we determine the complete Walsh distribution of the balanced Boolean function $f_λ$ parameterized by $P_λ(x+x^2)$ and prove that this distribution is independent of $λ$. For $m\geq3$, these functions have the five-valued Walsh spectrum ${q,0,-q,-2q,-3q}$, while for $m=2$ the spectrum degenerates to four values. As applications, their supports yield projective minimal binary five-weight codes, sets with five hyperplane intersection numbers, and regular cubelike Cayley graphs with six distinct eigenvalues. Finally, for mappings of the form $P(x+x^{-1})$, we construct an infinite family of balanced Boolean functions with simple explicit trace representations.

items.title: Linear Convergence of Adaptive Accelerated Gradient Methods: A Unified Framework
items.summary: We establish a unified Lyapunov framework for adaptive accelerated gradient methods on smooth, strongly convex objectives. Conditions on local curvature, stepsize ratios, and coefficient variation ensure eventual linear convergence without assuming stepsize convergence. We verify these conditions for specified AdaNAG-G, smooth unconstrained AC-FGM, and AdaAGM policies and use them to design VC-FG and CC-FG. The verified adaptive main iterations require neither global smoothness nor strong-convexity parameters and avoid restart and backtracking. The framework also sharpens a fixed-step FISTA/NAG-type bound. Experiments on four smooth, strongly convex problem families illustrate complementary performance of the new methods.

items.title: Gradient-based optimization of buoyancy distributions for lazy-wave risers
items.summary: This paper presents a novel gradient-based approach for optimizing the buoyancy distribution of lazy-wave offshore risers. The static response is modeled with a total potential energy formulation for a geometrically nonlinear, inextensible beam on an elastic seabed. The total potential energy is discretized by finite differences and the resulting nonlinear equilibrium system is solved by a two stage continuation procedure, in which the line length and then the buoyancy load are increased incrementally, with Newton--Raphson iterations and an Armijo line search. The design variables are the uplift ratios at the nodes where buoyancy modules may be installed. The optimization minimizes a quadratic measure of buoyancy demand subject to constraints on the maximum curvature and effective tension. The gradients of the constraints are computed by means of a discrete adjoint sensitivity analysis. Three design parametrizations are compared: a continuous formulation with independent nodal uplift ratios, a grouped formulation with fixed module assignments, and a formulation inspired by discrete material optimization that simultaneously selects the uplift ratios of a small catalog of module types and their placement along the riser. The latter yields practical designs with a limited number of module sizes. The framework provides a flexible and computationally efficient tool for preliminary design of lazy-wave configurations.

items.title: A 3D PINN-Based Framework for Patient-Specific Pulmonary Hemodynamics Using Windkessel Models
items.summary: Cardiovascular fluid dynamics modeling relies heavily on mesh-based numerical methods such as Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). While accurate, these methods entail significant computational costs and complex meshing workflows that limit their translation to clinical practice. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) are a promising meshless alternative that embeds the governing equations directly into neural network training. In this work, we propose a PINN framework for pulsatile blood flow in patient-specific geometries with dynamic lumped-parameter Windkessel (RCR) outlet conditions representing distal vascular impedance. Coupling the Windkessel ODE to a 3D network raises two difficulties: the ODE alone does not fix the pressure level, and the local pressure variations that drive the flow are orders of magnitude smaller than the basal pressure imposed by the outlet. We address them by decomposing pressure into a time-dependent basal part and a spatially varying part, an initial condition and gauge for the Windkessel equation, a global mass-balance constraint, and a periodic Fourier embedding of time. Validated on 2D canonical channels (steady and pulsatile, with and without RCR outlet), the framework is then applied to a patient-specific right pulmonary artery, reproducing outlet flow, mean pressure, and the velocity and dynamic pressure fields with errors on the order of the data resolution. Finally, we solve the inverse problem of identifying the three Windkessel parameters of the outlet from synthetic data, recovering them with errors of about 0.3% from deliberately wrong initial values. Residual biases in the local pressure field and the need to test robustness to noisy clinical data remain open, but the results support PINNs as complementary tools for meshless hemodynamics and patient-specific digital twins.

items.title: A Validation-Driven Bilevel Optimization Method for Mesh-Free PDE Solvers and Its Error Analysis
items.summary: Mesh-free partial differential equation (PDE) solvers construct discrete systems from residuals at sampled points. These solvers fit coefficients in a parameterized trial representation and select solver-design parameters governing the representation, training-residual weighting, and regularization. These parameters strongly affect solution accuracy, yet existing selection strategies are largely tailored to particular solver classes. To address this limitation, we formulate a unified validation-driven bilevel optimization framework applicable across different solver classes, in which the lower level fits coefficients using training collocation residuals, while the upper level selects solver-design parameters using held-out validation residuals. For nonlinear PDEs, however, solving the nonlinear lower-level problem to high accuracy is costly, while the adjoint system is typically ill-conditioned and indefinite. To address this issue, we propose an efficient implicit hypergradient method that approximates the lower-level response using finite, warm-started damped Gauss-Newton (GN) updates. For the adjoint solve, we use the damped GN matrix to compute an initial adjoint and to precondition a finite number of minimum residual iterations. To quantify the errors introduced by these approximations, we derive local hypergradient error bounds that separate the contributions of the finite lower-level solve, adjoint damping, and the final adjoint residual. Combining this analysis with validation sampling bounds and residual stability, we relate validation residuals to PDE solution accuracy and establish error bounds for the computed PDE solution. Numerical experiments on several nonlinear PDEs, including a high-dimensional problem, demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method across Kansa, random feature and extreme learning machine, and physics-informed neural network solvers.

items.title: Dual-Agent DRL based Cooperative Beamforming and Trajectory Optimization for UAV-ISAC Networks
items.summary: This paper considers a low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) network, where multiple ground base stations (BSs) provide integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) services for multiple communication UAVs (C-UAVs) and sensing UAVs (S-UAVs). With the objective of maximizing the average sum rate of C-UAVs over the entire flight episode, we jointly optimize the multi-BS multi-UAV ISAC beamforming and trajectory design, subject to the BS transmit power budget and the sensing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints of S-UAVs, as well as the flight mission and collision avoidance constraints of C-UAVs and S-UAVs. Based on the multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) technique, we develop a dual-agent scheme, termed DeepDA-OPT, to solve the resulting constrained Markov decision process (MDP). In the proposed DeepDA-OPT scheme, two agents, i.e., Agent-B and Agent-T, are specifically deployed for learning the multi-BS ISAC transmit beamformers and the C-UAV/S-UAV trajectories, respectively, where the optimal BS receive beamformers for the sensing echo signals of S-UAVs are obtained in closed form by leveraging the generalized Rayleigh quotient theorem. To mitigate the overestimation of value functions, both Agent-B and Agent-T are trained based on the twin-delayed deep deterministic (TD3) policy-gradient algorithm. In addition, a constraint-aware noise exploration policy is employed, and the reward function is designed to incorporate a sensing penalty and a flight urgency penalty, thereby guiding the training of Agent-B and Agent-T. Numerical results show that, compared with the baseline schemes, the proposed DeepDA-OPT scheme achieves a higher average sum rate of C-UAVs, while the sensing SINR constraints are empirically well satisfied and no collision violation is observed under the evaluated settings.

items.title: Karcher means of structured matrices are asymptotically structured: a study via Schatten estimates for the additive Richardson iteration
items.summary: In the present work, we first study the additive Richardson iteration for the Karcher mean of complex Hermitian positive definite (HPD) matrix sequences, by obtaining normalized Schatten estimates independent of the matrix dimension. These estimates are used to prove that Karcher means of structured matrices are asymptotically structured and this is proven for input HPD Toeplitz and generalized locally Toeplitz (GLT) matrix sequences. More precisely, we provide the a.c.s. approximation, which is the key for demonstrating the GLT closure under Schatten spectral bounds, and the GLT conclusion can be extended to matrix sequences with symbols that are positive definite almost everywhere. Ad hoc numerical experiments illustrate the spectral distribution consequences of these results and few related computational advantages. Concluding remarks and open problems are provided in the final section.

items.title: A fast automatically adaptive integral equation solver for nonlinear two-point boundary value systems
items.summary: We present a fast, high-order, automatically adaptive integral-equation solver for nonlinear two-point boundary value systems. The method builds on the fast direct solver for linear second-kind integral equations and completes the mathematical formulation needed for general boundary conditions, including cases in which the simplest background Green's function is singular and cases with genuinely rank-deficient boundary conditions. Nonlinear problems are written as nonlinear second-kind integral equations and are solved by combining this fast adaptive linear solver with Newton iteration and user-specified continuation. In this way the nonlinear solver inherits the full strengths of the linear integral-equation method: a fast direct solver, arbitrary order accuracy, and automatic adaptive resolution with only a small overhead over a solve on the final mesh. The resulting algorithm is particularly effective for problems with localized or multiscale structure, including boundary layers, dense oscillations, transition regions, hypersensitive optimal-control systems, and singular perturbations. The same framework also provides a computational foundation for future studies of bifurcation and solution-branch exploration.

items.title: Two-phase visco-elastic FENE-P model: Thermodynamically consistent modeling, sharp interface limit analysis and unconditionally energy stable numerical scheme
items.summary: Although mathematical modeling and numerical simulations for two-phase Newtonian flows have been extensively studied for many years, relatively little work has focused on developing thermodynamically consistent models for two-phase Non-Newtonian viscoelastic flows, and to the author's best konowledge, no structure-preserving numerical methods have been reported for such models. In this paper, we focus on modeling the two-phase non-Newtonnian visco-elastic FENE-P model based on the energetic variational approach (EnVarA). In the model, a phase-field function is introduced to describe the diffuse interface which satisfies the Cahn-Hilliard (CH) equation. And all the physical variables can be connected smoothly. We conduct a matched asymptotic analysis for the sharp interface limit, which shows the diffuse interface model will converge to the sharp interface model when the interface thickness trends to zero. We then reformulate the model in an equivalent form that facilitates the construction of the numerical scheme. A weakly decoupled scheme is proposed for the resulting FENE-P-CH system, and its unconditional energy stability is proved theoretically. Finally, a series of numerical experiments is conducted to validate the model and assess the performance of the proposed scheme.

items.title: From data pencils to image representations of continuous-time LTI systems
items.summary: The continuous-time fundamental lemma describes the set of all trajectories of a linear time-invariant system by a Gramian matrix built from measured input--output data and their derivatives. The jet of a trajectory is represented as the Gramian applied to a nonunique parameter satisfying a differential-algebraic equation. We determine the complete Kronecker structure of the associated data pencil for multiple-input multiple-output systems. This enables the construction of a polynomial image representation of the input--output behavior directly from the data. The resulting image matrix has column degrees equal to the controllability indices, and its latent variable is free and serves as a flat output of the system. The computation relies on an orthogonal staircase reduction followed by basis reconstruction using polynomial kernels. We also propose a structure-preserving preconditioning of the Gramian to improve its condition number and facilitate rank decisions in the reduction. We illustrate our approach on a chain of mass-spring-damper systems.

items.title: Error-Corrected Physics-Informed Neural Operator for Optimal Control of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles under Uncertainty
items.summary: We solve open-loop optimal control problems under parametric uncertainty using a physics-informed DeepONet that returns trajectories for all sampled scenarios in one evaluation. Trained only on the residual at generic controls, the operator is reused across targets and horizons. Because a gradient-based optimizer exploits surrogate errors, we correct the prediction by one Newton step on the dynamics, computed for all scenarios and times by one parallel scan. The corrected state has a second-order error bounded by the residual alone, and the corrected cost is honest for every control up to the sampling error. On a fixed-wing UAV benchmark, the corrected operator matches the accuracy of a batched Adam solver and an Ipopt solver at equal sample size and is 8 times faster than the Adam solver on the same GPU at a few hundred scenarios and 15 times faster than Ipopt on a CPU.

items.title: Stinespring's Dilation, Universal-NOT, and Limitations of Quantum Uncoupled Learning
items.summary: Uncoupled learning, in which players know only their own payoff, are a standard model of decentralized learning toward Nash equilibrium. We study their quantum counterpart, where strategies are quantum states and, in each round, a player receives a physical copy of their opponent's current strategy and updates their own state by a quantum channel. This adds to uncoupledness a constraint with no classical analogue: every update must be physically realizable. In fact, this constraint is decisive in conjugation games, in which Bob has a strictly dominant pure strategy and Alice's unique best response is its transpose. In this work, we show some limitations of uncoupled (learning) dynamics in finding the Nash equilibrium for conjugation games. First, we prove that no autonomous, memoryless, uncoupled dynamics converge to Nash equilibrium in a family of four single-qubit conjugation games. Specifically, any memoryless channel that keeps all four equilibria fixed will leave Alice's strategy frozen. This result also extends to $4^n$ games on $n$-qubit registers. Second, we show that this barrier disappears with a small classical memory: for any finite family of $L$ pure targets, a guess-and-test rule with $O(\log L)$ classical bits converges to equilibrium, with an explicit bound on its convergence rate. Finally, we prove that no finite memory, classical or quantum, suffices for the continuum of all pure-qubit targets. Our proof of the impossibility for memoryless channels relies on Stinespring's dilation theorem, while the impossibility for finite-memory channels relies on the optimal universal-NOT (in)fidelity bound by Bužek, Hillery, and Werner.

items.title: Parareal Approximation of Stochastic $L^2$-Boosting
items.summary: We study Parareal approximations of stochastic \(L^2\)-boosting, reusing the learner draws of the sequential algorithm in the fine propagators. We establish mean-square error bounds whose order improves with each correction, characterize the limiting distributions of normalized errors, including non-Gaussian components and the effects of coarse discretization, and derive sufficient conditions for preserving the statistical limit laws and validation-based stopping behavior of the sequential algorithm. Numerical experiments with sample-dependent coordinate and nonlinear residual-fitting learners examine the predicted convergence rates and limiting distributions, while computational benchmarks assess the efficiency of the method relative to sequential implementations.

items.title: Tight Logarithmic Separations between LZ77 and LZRR
items.summary: LZRR is a copy-based lossless compression method that produces a bidirectional macro scheme. It greedily parses a string from left to right. At each step, it can copy from an occurrence on either side of the current position, provided that the copy creates no cycle. Let $z$ and $z_{\mathrm{RR}}$ denote the sizes of the LZ77 and LZRR parsings, respectively. Under the original LZRR rule, we show that $z/z_{\mathrm{RR}}=Θ(\log n)$ on a family of Fibonacci words and that $z_{\mathrm{RR}}/z=Θ(\log n)$ on a family based on bit reversal, where $n$ is the string length. The Fibonacci separation holds under every tie-breaking rule. Both separations are asymptotically tight.

items.title: When Speed Changes Where to Build: Optimal Placement of an Optional Fast Connection
items.summary: Express roads, limited-stop transit, and air taxis speed up only the trips that choose them, while others stay on the ground network. Where should such a connection's terminals go? Because its users change with the design, expected travel time is nonconvex and nonsmooth in the terminal locations. Previous models have therefore been solved numerically or in restricted settings. We solve a canonical case exactly: uniform trips in a square with grid streets and a straight link. We find that every optimal design is centered and diagonal or axis aligned, and the alignment switches once, near 2.18 times ground speed. The two designs tied there differ sharply in coverage and ridership. A planner also choosing speed, at a smooth cost of speed, never selects the switching speed. If the cost is proportional to speed, above a threshold unit cost the planner builds a slower diagonal link, below it a faster axis-aligned one, and the optimal speed skips a band around the switch. On a rectangle, every optimum is again centered, centered designs have a closed-form travel time, and only two families of links can be optimal, those along the long axis and those tilted toward the long side.

items.title: Balanced Divide and Conquer for Rooted Maximum Agreement Forests
items.summary: We develop a balanced divide-and-conquer framework for the maximum agreement forest problem on rooted binary phylogenetic tree--forest instances. The goal is a common subforest with the fewest components; budget $k$ bounds the increase relative to the input forest. We balance edges associated with an unknown optimum to obtain three subproblems with smaller budgets. Branching separates the inputs, while temporary marker leaves allow a global optimum to be recovered from independently computed optimal solutions. For any fixed $B>\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$, the framework converts a tree--forest solver running in $O^*(B^k)$ time into one running in $O^*((\sqrt{\varphi B})^k)$ time. Starting from an $O^*(2.3391^k)$-time solver, two applications yield an $O^*(1.7743^{k^*})$-time fixed-parameter algorithm for two trees, where $k^*$ is the number of components in a maximum agreement forest minus one. For every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, a fixed number of applications yields $O^*((\varphi+\varepsilon)^{k^*})$ time. Here $O^*$ suppresses polynomial factors, whose degree and constants may depend on $\varepsilon$.

items.title: A Higher-Order Algorithm for Solving Time-Fractional Differential Equations via Rational Approximation of z^α as a Herglotz-Nevanlinna function
items.summary: Time-Fractional derivatives (TFDs) have been widely used in mathematical modeling of physical phenomena such as anomalous diffusion and memory effects of materials. Traditionally, TFD is handled {either by a direct method which saves almost all the memory and hence computationally expensive or a sum of exponential method (SOE) which decomposes the time domain improper integral into a local term and a history term} {approximated by} a sum of exponential functions. The limitation of the SOE approach is that{ the approximation error of the local term might result in large errors if the unknown function is not smooth enough at $0$ and can lead to over-dissipation of energy.} In this paper, we take a different approach and will focus on the Caputo derivative because the Caputo time derivative of a constant function is 0. We present a simple time-stepping algorithm based on the theory of Stieltjes-Markov functions, a subclass of the Herglotz-Nevanlinna functions. The key is in identifying the Stieltjes-Markov function structure hidden in the Laplace transform of the kernel function. Compared to most of the current methods in literature, the novelty of the results in this paper is manifold. First, no decomposition of integral is needed and our resulting approximation in the time domain contains a Dirac measure with carefully calculated strength, leading to a drastic decrease in the number of exponential functions needed in the approximation. Secondly, the choice of our interpolation points is based on the Mellin's inversion theorem and hence the interpolation error in the transformed domain is explicitly and rigorously linked to the error in the time-domain. {Finally, the resulting system is almost diagonal and hence can be easily sped up by using the Schur complement method.}

items.title: Degree-stratified randomized projection for spectral clustering
items.summary: Many real-world networks have heavy-tailed degree distributions, in which a few high-degree nodes coexist with many low-degree nodes. Randomized range finders reduce the cost of computing the eigenspace used in spectral clustering, but their random test matrices are constructed independently of the node degrees. We propose degree-stratified randomized projection (DS-RP), which partitions the nodes into dyadic degree strata, distributes a fixed sketch dimension across the strata, and draws an independent local sketch for each stratum. We bound the angle between the sampled range and the target eigenspace and show that the gain comes from the allocation of the sketch dimension rather than from the stratification itself. The bound improves when more sketch dimensions are assigned to the strata on which the target eigenspace is concentrated. For the degree-corrected stochastic block model, we prove that the leverage scores of this eigenspace are proportional to the node degrees, so that the allocation can be determined from the degrees alone. A Rayleigh--Ritz bound that requires no smallness assumption carries the estimate over to the computed spectral embedding. Numerical experiments on synthetic benchmarks and real-world networks show that DS-RP improves the clustering accuracy of standard Gaussian and CountSketch projections at the same sketch dimension and essentially the same computational cost.

items.title: On the convergence of greedy algorithms in one-dimensional Wasserstein space
items.summary: We study the convergence of the greedy algorithm for approximating a compact set by barycenters in metric spaces, in particular in the space of one-dimensional measures endowed with the 2-Wasserstein distance. To this end, we compare several metric $N$-widths, which measure the best error achievable with $N$-point barycenters, using either classical barycenters having nonnegative weights or signed barycenters, with weights of arbitrary sign summing to one. For the analysis we exploit that quantile functions embed the one-dimensional 2-Wasserstein space isometrically into a convex cone of $L^2(0,1)$, and barycenter sets correspond to nonlinear projections of convex or affine hulls. We prove, both in the algebraic and exponential case, that the convergence rate of the greedy algorithm using signed barycenters matches the one of the metric $N$-width defined with classical barycenters. We provide counterexamples showing that this fails for the other combinations.

items.title: Online Learning for Minimizing Maximum Tardiness in Single-Machine Scheduling
items.summary: We study online learning for minimizing maximum tardiness (\OMMT) in single-machine scheduling. In each round, the learner selects a permutation of \(n\) fixed jobs, representing a schedule. The environment then reveals a processing time and a due date for each job, and the learner incurs a vector-valued loss whose components correspond to the tardiness of the individual jobs. The goal of the learner is to minimize \(α\)-regret, the difference between the learner's maximum cumulative tardiness and \(α\) times that of the best fixed permutation in hindsight, for as small \(α\) as possible. We investigate OMMT under both stochastic and adversarial environments. In the stochastic setting, we prove that the expected \(1\)-regret of the Follow-the-Leader (FTL) algorithm is \( O\!\left(\frac{n\log n}{Δ^2}\right) \), together with a corresponding high-probability bound, where \(Δ\) is a distribution-dependent gap parameter. At round \(t \in \{1,\dots,T\}\), FTL runs in \(O(tn^2)\) time and \(O(tn)\) space. In the adversarial setting, we prove that, for any \(0<c<\log_2 n/16\), the \(α\)-regret is \(Ω(T)\) whenever \(α<\log_2 n/16-c\). We then reduce OMMT to a surrogate online learning problem and apply Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader (FTPL), obtaining an expected \(α\)-regret bound of \(O(n^2\sqrt{T})\) for \(α=O(\log n)\). Thus, the logarithmic dependence of \(α\) on \(n\) is tight up to constant factors. Each FTPL update admits a mixed-integer programming formulation whose size is polynomial in \(n\) and \(t\).

items.title: Distribution-Robust Halfspace Testing
items.summary: Standard property testing algorithms are typically designed either for a specific input distribution (distribution-specific algorithms) or for an arbitrary unknown distribution (distribution-free algorithms). Halfspaces are an important example where distribution-specific testers can be extremely efficient, while distribution-free testers are expensive and essentially require learning. We introduce an intermediate type of algorithm, a distribution-robust halfspace tester, which must provide the same guarantees as a distribution-specific tester when the input distribution is the one specified, but must also provide a trustworthy answer under arbitrary distributions. This is achieved by allowing the tester to report that its input distribution is not what it expected (inspired by the recent testable learning framework of Rubinfeld and Vasilyan). We prove that distribution-robust testing of halfspaces under the standard Gaussian requires only $O(n^{2/3})$ queries, compared to the known $\widetilde Ω(n)$ required for distribution-free testing. We also prove that sample-based distribution-robust testing of halfspaces is harder than sample-based testing under the standard Gaussian, requiring at least $Ω(n^{2/3})$ samples compared to the known $\widetilde Θ(\sqrt n)$ bound for the latter. In fact, we show that the latter $\widetilde Θ(\sqrt n)$ bound becomes $Ω(n^{2/3})$ when the covariance matrix is only mildly perturbed.

items.title: Inverse scattering for the one-dimensional discrete Schrödinger operator: a computational perspective
items.summary: We revisit inverse scattering for the one-dimensional discrete Schrödinger operator with compactly supported perturbation. We consider a computational perspective, adapted to the case of a digitally sampled reflection coefficient, to determine the perturbation in the form of a Jacobi matrix, including a computation of the length of the smallest interval supporting the perturbation. A new representation of scattering data in terms of orthogonal polynomials underpins the computational results. A key technical role is played by polynomials on the circle constructed from pairs of successive orthogonal polynomials on the line. The inverse algorithm is demonstrated on numerical examples.

items.title: Carleman estimates and $φ$-null controllability for a fully discrete fourth-order parabolic equation
items.summary: We consider a fully discrete approximation of a one-dimensional fourth-order parabolic equation with clamped boundary conditions, obtained by centered finite differences in space and the implicit Euler method in time, and controlled by two boundary controls acting at the left endpoint. We prove a Carleman estimate for the corresponding discrete adjoint operator, in which the large Carleman parameter is connected to the space and time discretization parameters $h$ and $Δt$. As a consequence, we obtain a relaxed observability inequality and a $φ(h)$-null controllability result, in which the controls are bounded uniformly with respect to $h$ and $Δt$, and the norm of the solution at the final time is of order $\sqrt{φ(h)}$, with $φ(h)$ exponentially small, provided $Δt\le h^μ$ for some $μ\ge1$.

items.title: Testable Testing: Distribution-Robust Property Testing
items.summary: We introduce a new model for property testing of Boolean functions, which we call distribution-robust testing. Distribution-robust testing is motivated by the hope of designing testers whose output can be trusted even when the underlying probability distribution does not satisfy the assumptions of the tester, while still being more efficient than distribution-free testers that make no assumptions at all. The purpose of this paper is to perform a broad initial exploration of this new model. In particular, we present a variety of general algorithmic techniques, which we apply to show that several well-studied properties admit distribution-robust testers that are significantly more efficient than their distribution-free counterparts. For example, we obtain constant-query distribution-robust testers for conjunctions, decision lists, and unions of intervals, all of which are known to require significantly more queries in the distribution-free model. These encouraging results suggest a range of questions for future work.

items.title: Fair Property Tax: Reducing Regressivity in Machine-Learning Valuation
items.summary: Advanced machine-learning models are increasingly used for property valuation in tax assessment. Although these models can achieve high predictive accuracy, they may systematically assign higher valuation-to-sale ratios to lower-priced properties, a pattern known as regressivity. In collaboration with the Cook County Assessor's Office (CCAO), we develop and evaluate two training methods that substantially reduce this regressive pattern while maintaining price-scale predictive accuracy. The Direct method has been incorporated into CCAO's public residential valuation software. Retaining the LightGBM model class used at CCAO, we propose a Direct penalty on squared covariance between log valuation errors and log sale prices, and an observation-additive Surrogate that yields a weighted squared-error loss. We evaluate both methods in our implementation of the CCAO workflow, using seven chronological validation folds, a held-out test set, and a 2025-forward test set. Measured by the magnitude of price-related bias (PRB), regressivity falls by approximately 49% on held-out sales and 39% on 2025 sales at a Surrogate setting selected by cross-validation, relative to the same LightGBM model fitted without the penalty. Price-scale $R^2$ is essentially unchanged. Its small rise, from 0.893 to 0.897 on held-out sales and from 0.904 to 0.908 on 2025 sales, reflects overall valuation level. Log-price RMSE rises by 3.1% and 1.7%, respectively. Paired sale-bootstrap 90% intervals for the PRB reductions lie within about two percentage points of these estimates. In an additional eight-county benchmark, both methods reduce regressivity in every county, with higher log-price prediction error as the expected tradeoff. These findings demonstrate a practical way to reduce measured regressivity within an existing assessor workflow while preserving price-scale predictive performance.

items.title: A linearly decoupled structure-preserving BCFD method for the two-species Keller--Segel chemotaxis system
items.summary: In this paper, we develop a fully discrete, linearly decoupled block-centered finite difference scheme for the two-species Keller--Segel chemotaxis system. Based on the Slotboom transformation, the cell-density equations are reformulated into a symmetric form, providing a natural framework for the construction of a structure-preserving discretization. The resulting scheme is shown to unconditionally preserve the positivity of both the cell densities and the chemoattractant concentration, while ensuring exact mass conservation of each cell density and the original energy dissipation. Furthermore, optimal-order error estimates for the proposed scheme are rigorously established through a higher-order consistency analysis. In particular, the cell densities exhibit first-order temporal and second-order spatial convergence in the discrete $L^2$-norm, whereas the chemoattractant concentration achieves the same convergence orders in the discrete $H^1$-norm. Finally, a series of numerical experiments is conducted to verify the theoretical results and demonstrate the reliability of the proposed scheme in simulating the finite-time blow-up phenomenon.

items.title: Semi-regular admixed arrays: asymptotic enumeration and when information is additive
items.summary: In genomic data analysis, admixed arrays are pairs of matrices recording the local ancestry and the allele at each position of the haplotypes of admixed individuals. We study two-way diploid admixed arrays with $N$ individuals and $P$ loci under two families of constraints: local ancestry tallies, which fix the number of ancestry assignments per individual, and ancestry-specific sums, which fix the allele count per locus and ancestry. These two constraint families correspond to summaries of admixed genetic data investigated in biomedical and genomic applications. In the semi-regular regime, where all tallies and sums are uniform, we use complex martingale techniques to derive asymptotic formulas for the number of doubly constrained arrays as $N$ and $P$ grow with bounded ratio, over the whole feasible region. The leading term is governed by the Shannon entropy of the frequencies of the four possible pairs of entries at a position of the two matrices; on the boundary one or two of them vanish, changing the Gaussian correction. We then ask whether the two families carry information additively, that is, whether an independence heuristic predicts the doubly constrained count up to a bounded factor. Measured against the smallest set of arrays defined by a constraint that each family implies on its own, additivity holds only on a set of measure zero. It includes an edge of the feasible region with correction factor $e^{-1/4}$, extending our earlier result at the symmetric point. Thus, how far the two summaries jointly narrow down individual-level ancestry and genotype configurations cannot generally be predicted from how far each does on its own.

items.title: Subspace Inference for Multilayer Latent Space Networks: Intrinsic Geometry and One-Step Estimator
items.summary: Multilayer networks on a common node set, such as brain connectomes of several animals with one layer per animal, often share a low-dimensional geometry but differ in how strongly each layer expresses it and in node activity. We study a multilayer latent space network model that combines an invariant subspace common to all layers with layer-specific interaction matrices and node-by-layer degree effects. By introducing the generalized Cayley transform of the invariant subspace, we characterize the intrinsic geometry of the model and obtain sharp convergence rates for the maximum likelihood estimator, asymptotic normality and Neyman orthogonality for vertex-level parameters, and asymptotic normality for the interaction matrices with a non-negligible bias. Plug-in estimates of the bias and covariance give debiased confidence regions and tests of equality between layers. We also propose an easy-to-implement one-step estimator that attains the same vertex-level limits. In a real-world mouse connectome dataset, the inbred strain that lacks a corpus callosum shows about twice the hemispheric segregation of the other three strains.

items.title: A Stochastic Tamed-Regularized Random Batch Method for Uncertain Particle Systems with Singularities
items.summary: The coefficients of particle systems often exhibit uncertainties due to incomplete knowledge. For particle systems with uncertainties and singularities in the drift and diffusion terms, existing methods may encounter numerical blow-up. In this paper, we propose a novel stochastic tamed-regularized Random Batch (str-RB) method for such uncertain particle systems with singularities. Specifically, since singularities in the diffusion term are more challenging than those in the drift term, building on a tamed scheme, we design an exponential regularization strategy that more effectively mitigates singularities in the diffusion term. This strategy ensures that the stochastic Galerkin (sG) projection coefficients remain finite even when the corresponding integrals for the original singular diffusion coefficient diverge. The sG method is applied to handle the random coefficients, and a random batch approach is then employed to reduce the computational complexity of large-scale simulations. Several theoretical properties of the proposed algorithm are established. Numerical tests demonstrate that the str-RB algorithm exhibits weak convergence, achieves lower errors than major existing methods across singular tests, and remains stable in a wider range of singular regimes. This work provides a robust and accurate approach for uncertain particle systems with singularities, laying a foundation for high-performance solvers in uncertain many-body dynamics.

items.title: Spectral Estimation with Deformed Decompression
items.summary: Sample covariance matrices are fundamental objects in machine learning and statistics, with valuable information encoded into their eigenvalues. When treating modern problems, the scale of these matrices can become prohibitive for tractable computation. This creates a critical need for "spectral decompression": a method for inferring the eigenspectrum of a very large-scale model using only information from its smaller realizations. Existing methods fall into two main categories: those relying on spectral inversion; and those that rely on Free Decompression techniques. On the one hand, spectral inversion is a fundamentally ill-posed problem that is notoriously unstable, often failing to yield reliable results in finite-size settings. On the other hand, while Free Decompression was recently proposed to address this scaling, its reliance on the Nica-Speicher framework restricts its use to unitarily invariant ensembles, a symmetry condition that subsampled covariance matrices fail to satisfy. In this work, we introduce Deformed Decompression (DD), a novel framework for the stable, forward-extrapolation of spectral densities. By leveraging properties of the companion matrix, DD recasts the spectral decompression problem as a directed evolution of the Stieltjes transform of the companion matrix. This approach bypasses the instabilities of traditional inversion and provides a robust methodology for scaling covariance matrices and even their generalized variants (including Hessian matrices) that lack unitary invariance. We demonstrate the utility of our framework through experiments on a variety of random matrix examples, showing that DD successfully captures the complex spectral signatures of large-scale systems.

items.title: Semigroup Hessian Estimates for Underdamped Langevin Dynamics
items.summary:
For the semigroup $e^{t\mathcal L}$ of the underdamped Langevin dynamics, we bound the Hessian $
abla^2(e^{t\mathcal L}f)$ when $
abla f$ is uniformly bounded. When the potential is strongly convex outside a ball and has bounded second and third derivatives, and the damping rate is above an explicit threshold, the bounds on $
abla^2(e^{t\mathcal L}f)$ decay exponentially in time with constants free of the dimension. The proof combines the Wasserstein contraction of the dynamics with a Bismut--Elworthy--Li formula for the degenerate noise. As an application, we prove the uniform-in-time error of the stochastic gradient UBU integrator, with an explicit coefficient of the numerical bias in the step size, proportional to the covariance of the stochastic gradient noise.

items.title: Uncovering Multimorbidity Patterns Through a Novel Randomized Clustering Algorithm
items.summary: Patients with several chronic conditions rarely share the same combination: in four years of the nationally representative Medical Expenditure Panel Survey (MEPS), we find 32,789 distinct combinations of two to seven conditions, and over 90% of those involving four or more occur in a single patient. Methods that search for common combinations discard most of this heterogeneity. We present the Randomized Length Sequential Clustering Algorithm (RLSCA), which links diseases by lift, a pairwise association measure counted only above a user-set support threshold. A mixed-integer program repeatedly selects and removes the group of conditions with the greatest internal lift, up to a random size; 100 iterations yield a database of clusters scored by size, rediscovery frequency, and body systems spanned. In MEPS 2019, stratified by age and sex, RLSCA recovers known groupings at a high threshold, such as diabetes with lipid disorders and hypertension, and at a lower threshold returns clusters of up to eight conditions spanning five body systems. Frequent itemset mining, at its lowest feasible support, finds no set above five conditions; hierarchical clustering cannot control cluster size. With a clinical large language model, the database could suggest which further conditions a patient is at risk of.

items.title: AI-Assisted Decision Support for Formula 1 Pit-Stop Strategy: Deep Reinforcement Learning and Mathematical Programming
items.summary: Pit-stop strategy in Formula 1 is a sequential decision problem under uncertainty, in which strategists decide at each lap whether to pit and which tire compound to fit. We develop a data-driven simulator, calibrated with historical race data, that captures tire degradation, drivers' recent performance, overtaking, yellow flag events, and rivals' pit-stop decisions. We train agents with five Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithms and compare them with a Quadratic Mixed-Integer Programming (QMIP) formulation that is optimal in deterministic single-driver settings. Without uncertainty or competition, all DRL methods except TRPO achieve near-optimal performance. With a full grid of competitors and stochastic race events, the ranking of DRL methods depends on the evaluation setting: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and its recurrent variant are the only methods that improve on the QMIP both in fully simulated races and when the actual 2024 races are replayed. Averaged over eight circuits, PPO improves on the QMIP by 0.33 and 0.49 positions in the two settings and Recurrent PPO by less, and in the replay PPO finishes 0.66 positions ahead of the drivers' actual strategies simulated in the same races. The QMIP performs similarly to the other methods, even though it cannot anticipate yellow flag events. Finally, we use the trained PPO policy as a look-ahead decision-support tool that shows the strategist the distribution of race outcomes under each candidate pit-stop action. Applied retrospectively to eight 2024 races, the look-ahead identifies the laps where the actual decision, the recommendation, or a third action was preferable.

items.title: Estimating contextual networks via Fisher-scoring surrogate likelihood
items.summary: When networks are accompanied by vertex-level covariates, effectively integrating and aligning the information underlying both data sources becomes a natural yet critical task. Current spectral approaches, despite their popularity, may yield suboptimal results and necessitate the specification of additional tuning parameters that are contingent upon unobservable signal-to-noise ratios. We propose a tuning-free, likelihood-based learning framework for estimating latent positions in contextual generalized random dot product graphs in the presence of high-dimensional vertex covariates with a low-rank structure. Our method constructs a smooth surrogate likelihood and implements a Fisher-scoring algorithm to iteratively estimate latent positions without introducing additional tuning parameters that depend on the network sparsity. We establish the consistency and asymptotic normality of the Fisher-scoring estimator. Application to real-world data further demonstrates the method's practical utility, offering a principled and scalable alternative to spectral approaches for analyzing contextual networks in high-dimensional settings.

items.title: Inexact Proximal Method on Hadamard Manifolds
items.summary: We propose and analyze two inexact proximal point methods for unconstrained geodesically convex optimization on Hadamard manifolds. The first, a standard inexact proximal point method (SIPPM), accepts approximate subproblem solutions directly as new iterates and applies to arbitrary Hadamard manifolds under a summability condition on the relative error tolerances. The second, a hybrid inexact proximal point method (IHPPM), augments each inexact proximal step with a metric projection onto a half-space-like separating set, allowing the summability requirement to be relaxed to a fixed relative error tolerance at the cost of assuming geodesic convexity of the separating sets. For both methods we establish full asymptotic convergence, global $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-2})$ iteration-complexity bounds for approximate stationarity, and, under a local growth condition, local $Q$-linear convergence rates---with $Q$-superlinear acceleration for SIPPM when the proximal parameters tend to zero and a refined contraction factor for IHPPM. We further prove that the geodesic convexity of the separating sets holds automatically on Hadamard surfaces and on Hadamard manifolds of constant sectional curvature.

items.title: Testability of Homomorphism Inadmissibility: Property Testing Meets Database Theory
items.summary: In this paper, we utilize the perspective of property testing to consider the testability of relational database queries. A primary motivation is the desire to avoid reading an entire database to decide a property thereof. We focus on conjunctive queries, which are the most basic and heavily studied database queries. Each conjunctive query can be represented as a relational structure $\mathbf{A}$ such that deciding if the conjunctive query is satisfied by a relational structure $\mathbf{B}$ is equivalent to deciding if there exists a homomorphism from $\mathbf{A}$ to $\mathbf{B}$. We phrase our results in terms of homomorphisms. Precisely, we study, for each relational structure $\mathbf{A}$, the testability of homomorphism inadmissibility from $\mathbf{A}$. We consider algorithms that have oracle access to an input relational structure $\mathbf{B}$ and that distinguish, with high probability, the case where there is no homomorphism from $\mathbf{A}$ to $\mathbf{B}$, from the case where one needs to remove a constant fraction of tuples from $\mathbf{B}$ in order to suppress all such homomorphisms. We provide a complete characterization of the structures $\mathbf{A}$ from which one can test homomorphism inadmissibility with one-sided error by making a constant number of queries to $\mathbf{B}$. Our characterization shows that homomorphism inadmissibility from $\mathbf{A}$ is constant-query testable with one-sided error if and only if the core of $\mathbf{A}$ is $α$-acyclic. We also show that the injective version of the problem is constant-query testable with one-sided error if $\mathbf{A}$ is $α$-acyclic; this result generalizes existing results for testing subgraph-freeness in the general graph model.

items.title: Optimized solver algorithms for computing $\mathrm{Tr}(A^{-1})$
items.summary: Estimating the trace of the inverse of a large quark matrix is a longstanding problem in lattice QCD. The standard approach is Hutchinson's method, which uses random noise vectors to estimate the trace to a desired statistical tolerance. Each noise vector $b$ requires solving a system of linear equations $Ax = b$. In this work, we introduce a new class of Krylov solvers for this task, called Twin methods. Twin methods generate the Krylov polynomial once then reuse it on all other right-hand sides. This reduces the number of basic linear algebra operations in the algorithm and therefore lowers the trace computation time. We apply the Twin approach to BiCG and BiCGStab and test them on lattice QCD matrices of varying size and in a range of computing contexts. We also present a more economical estimation of $\mathrm{Tr}(A^{-1})$ which implements a polynomial approximation of $A^{-1}$ and a singular value deflation. In this scheme, the solvers are applied to only a few noise vectors, and the remainder are treated by the polynomial and the deflation. In our tests, the polynomial approximation combined with the deflation yield a 17-fold speedup in the time required to compute the trace over standard Hutchinson's method.

items.title: Exact Online $Q_n$ Estimation: Exploiting Sliding-Window Rank Invariance
items.summary: The $Q_n$ scale estimator (Rousseeuw and Croux, 1993) combines a 50% finite-sample breakdown point with high Gaussian efficiency, but its computation requires selecting an order statistic among the $\binom{n}{2}$ pairwise distances. We study exact online $Q_n$ computation in a sliding window by exploiting temporal rank coherence between consecutive windows. Formalizing the multiset decomposition of surviving pairwise distances in terms of strict and weak rank counts, we derive a tie-exact dual-rank update that verifies whether the previous unscaled estimate remains valid in $\mathcal{O}(\log n)$ comparisons while maintaining the sorted window in $\mathcal{O}(n)$ time. When the target rank shifts by $m$ positions, a localized row-heap procedure initialized via a monotonic two-pointer frontier scan extracts the new exact order statistic in $\mathcal{O}(n + m\log n)$ comparisons without materializing the difference matrix, complemented by a hybrid fallback that executes frontier-guided implicit matrix selection in $\mathcal{O}(n\log n)$ time for larger rank shifts. On deterministic multi-regime stress streams, our implementation matches the offline batch reference. In repeated same-platform benchmarks on a synthetic Gaussian stream, our implementation achieves median internal throughputs from 2,220,000 updates/s ($n=25$) and 1,140,000 updates/s ($n=51$) to 127,000 updates/s ($n=201$), outperforming both the exact FQN baseline ($2.5\times$ to $6.4\times$) and the approximate AFQN sketch ($1.3\times$ to $2.7\times$) across all tested window sizes.

items.title: Revisiting Generalized Median Estimators: Exact Bitwise Computation and Gray Code Acceleration
items.summary: Generalized median estimators evaluate the median of a symmetric kernel over all $M = \binom{n}{k}$ subsets of size $k$. Exhaustive evaluation was considered impractical even for $n = 29, k = 5$ ($M = 118,755$), prompting stochastic subsampling (Wilde and Grimshaw, 2013). We show that this barrier is computational, not combinatorial: storing all subsets requires $Θ(kM)$ space, whereas stateful enumeration uses $\mathcal{O}(k)$ auxiliary state and retains only $M$ kernel values. We combine two exhaustive traversals with three-way Quickselect and a deterministic median-of-medians fallback, giving worst-case $\mathcal{O}(M)$ selection. Gosper's successor takes $\mathcal{O}(k)$ kernel work per subset for $n < w$; a Revolving Door Gray code changes one element out and one in, enabling $\mathcal{O}(1)$ kernel updates between recalibrations and $\mathcal{O}(M + kM/P)$ total time. We derive floating-point error bounds for the location ($h_1$) and mean-centered sample variance ($h_2$) kernels and their resulting median. For $n = 29, k = 5$, our ANSI C implementation evaluates all $118,755$ subsets in $0.74$ ms and $0.71$ ms, respectively. A direct C sweep places the crossover with partial lexicographic unranking at approximately $18,000$-$23,000$ subsets ($15\%$-$19\%$ of $M$), below the $32,160$-$45,420$ subsets required by Wilde and Grimshaw's sequential approximation at $ε= 0.01$.

items.title: Polynomial sequences of Simplex pivots on 0/1-polytopes
items.summary: We study the number of Simplex pivots needed to solve linear programs over $0/1$-polytopes, starting from an arbitrary feasible basis and counting degenerate pivots. It has been known since the 1990s that from any extreme point of a 0/1-polytope there exists a monotone path of linear length to an optimal one.
